body:
hwcalib (simulator/cmd/hwcalib) fits the physics of a hardware profile to a sweep measured on one of your nodes, so the simulator draws what your machine draws instead of the builtin profiles’ vendor figures and placeholders. hwcalib sweep records the sweep on the node; hwcalib fit writes the result as a local profile the simulator loads from SIM_PROFILES_DIR.
Recording a sweep A sweep holds the node at a series of setpoints and records, at every sample, the node’s readings and the setpoints it held. Each setpoint needs at least 5 samples after it settles: with a 2 s sample period, 22 s or more.
Recording on the node with hwcalib sweep Run it on a drained node, as root (reading energy_uj and writing limits need root):
go build -o hwcalib ./simulator/cmd/hwcalib sudo ./hwcalib sweep -node <node> -write-limits -freq-max-mhz 2400,1900,1500 -out sweep.jsonl ./hwcalib fit -profile amd-epyc-2s-energy-only -node <node> sweep.jsonl The load is a duty-cycled spin on every logical CPU. The grid nests power limits, then frequency ceilings, then loads. Every file the sweep wrote is put back when it ends, also on an error or a signal. GPUs and host power are not swept.
Flag Default Meaning -node the host name the node name in the resource, which hwcalib fit -node picks -util 0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1 the loads, busy fractions of every CPU -freq-max-mhz (none) the scaling_max_freq ceilings, in MHz; needs -write-limits -power-limit-w (none) the package power limits, in W; needs -write-limits -write-limits false allow writing frequency ceilings and power limits -hold 30s how long each setpoint lasts -period 2s the sample period -duty-period 100ms the period of the duty-cycled load -sys-root, -proc-root /sys, /proc the trees to read and write -out - the file to write, - for standard output; an existing file is never replaced It exits 0 when the sweep completes, 1 on a read, write or interruption error, and 2 on a usage error.
Setpoints A sweep from another collector records each knob it holds as joulie.calibration.setpoint, one point per knob:
joulie.calibration.knob Value cpu.utilization busy fraction of every logical CPU, 0 to 1 cpu.frequency.max scaling_max_freq written to every cpufreq policy, in Hz cpu.power.limit package limit written to every package (RAPL PL1 or the HSMP socket cap), in W gpu.utilization busy fraction of every GPU, 0 to 1 gpu.power.limit limit written to every GPU, in W A utilization knob also carries joulie.calibration.class (such as cpu.compute_bound) and joulie.calibration.memory_intensity; the GPU fit needs them. The readings use the names of Simulator Metrics: hw.energy or hw.power per CPU package, DRAM zone and GPU, hw.host.energy, hw.cpu.speed, joulie.hw.power.limit and system.cpu.utilization.
File formats -format Input otlp (default) OTLP JSON Lines, one MetricsData per line, as the OpenTelemetry file exporter writes them; the resource names the node in k8s.node.name or host.name csv one node: a header row, then one row per point with time_unix_nano, metric, value, optional unit and start_time_unix_nano, and one column per point attribute Running a fit go build -o hwcalib ./simulator/cmd/hwcalib export SIM_PROFILES_DIR=/srv/joulie/profiles # outside any clone of this repository ./hwcalib fit -profile amd-epyc-2s-energy-only -node <node> sweep.jsonl Flag Default Meaning -profile (required) the profile the node is described by, builtin or local; it gives the topology and every parameter the sweep cannot fit -node (the only node) the node whose resource to read -format otlp otlp or csv -out-dir SIM_PROFILES_DIR where to write the fitted profile -name <profile>-measured the fitted profile’s name and file name -substep 0 the fixed physics substep of a simulated source, such as 100ms; 0 for hardware It prints one row per parameter (base value, fitted value, method, samples, or why it was not fitted), then what it assumed. It fits idle and peak CPU power and the analytic model’s exponents, DRAM and platform power, GPU idle and maximum power, and settling times. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 a sweep that cannot be read or fitted, 2 a usage error.
The fitted profile The fit writes <name>.yaml, which extends the base profile and holds only what the sweep measured. It is refused inside this repository (a measured profile may name your machine), never replaces an existing file, and is loaded back to check it. Name it in a cluster spec pool as any local profile (Simulator hardware profiles):
go run ./simulator/cmd/clusterspec validate -spec <spec.yaml> -profiles-dir /srv/joulie/profiles What a sweep reads and writes, how the sweep is cut into steady windows, every fit method and the substep correction: Hardware calibration on the wiki.

body:
This page says what Joulie models about CPUs and GPUs and where the numbers come from. The agent uses these facts to resolve caps; the simulator uses them to turn utilization and controls into power and slowdown.
In the simulator these models are a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: they rest on vendor figures, public measurements and assumptions. What meaningful experiments need is tracked in the milestone Evidence-based evaluation.
Validation status. Some catalog CPUs run public measured curves. GPU support is validated in simulation only. For GPUs and the other CPUs, the model combines official documentation with literature-based priors until direct calibration is possible.
Data provenance Every modelled value has one of three kinds of provenance; a proxy is never presented as a measurement.
Kind Examples Official or read at runtime CPU base and boost clocks, TDP and cTDP; GPU board power; cap ranges the node reports; CPU frequency landmarks and GPU clock ranges, which the agent publishes in NodeHardware (status.cpu.landmarks, status.gpu.governor.clockRangesMHz) as facts, not telemetry Public measured SPECpower node-level CPU power curves; published GPU throughput under power limits Proxy or inferred EPYC 9534 (from the 9654), EPYC 9375F (from the 9655), Xeon Gold 6530 (from an Intel family proxy); the simulator borrows no curve from a proxy, so these nodes run the analytic model Hardware inventory The catalog (pkg/hwinv/assets/hardware.yaml, read through pkg/hwinv/catalog.go) holds CPU and GPU entries, and a node is a discovered CPU model and count plus a GPU model and count. The agent, the controller manager and the simulator all read the same embedded copy, unless HARDWARE_CATALOG_PATH (SIM_HARDWARE_CATALOG_PATH for the simulator) replaces it. Model names are matched by alias after normalization.
The cluster inventory the experiments target:
Node GPUs CPUs GPU nodes NVIDIA H100 NVL 2x AMD EPYC 9654 NVIDIA H100 SXM 2x Intel Xeon Gold 6530 NVIDIA L40S 2x AMD EPYC 9534 AMD Instinct MI300X 2x AMD EPYC 9534 AMD Radeon Pro W7900 2x AMD EPYC 9534 Intel Data Center GPU Flex 170 2x Intel Xeon Gold 6530 CPU-only nodes none 2x AMD EPYC 9965, 2x AMD EPYC 9375F, 2x AMD EPYC 9655 Every entry, its vendor figures and its source are on the wiki page Hardware catalog.
Hardware not in the catalog Unknown hardware degrades realism; it does not break the control loop.
The CPU and the GPU fall back independently to the generic model, or to no throttling. The simulator fills four facts in a fixed order: the node class key, else the environment variable, else the catalog, else a built-in constant (the variables are in the configuration reference). An unknown GPU is capped between 80 and 300 W unless a class or a variable says otherwise. On a real node the agent still uses the cap limits the node reports. CPU model A CPU with a public SPECpower curve (2x EPYC 9654, 9655 and 9965) runs that curve; any other runs an analytic model, idle + (max - idle) x util^alpha x f^beta, with a peak of sockets x TDP for a catalog CPU. A cap lowers the frequency until the package meets it, settling as a first-order lag. Compute-bound work slows with the frequency; memory-bound work slows little until the frequency falls below a knee. Telemetry is averaged, and thermal throttling is opt-in. The equations, defaults and sources are on CPU power model.
GPU model Each physical GPU is modelled on its own, and a node’s GPU cap is the same per-device cap on every GPU. A workload has a natural power draw, lower for memory-bound work; a cap only matters once it falls below that draw. Under the cap, compute-bound work slows as ratio^computeGamma, fitted per family to published throughput (H100 SXM 0.43, H100 NVL 0.50, MI300X 0.62, L40S 1.20, others 1.0); memory-bound work slows less. Caps settle over a lag of 150 ms (350 ms on MI300X), and exported power is averaged over 1 s, as NVML reports it on NVIDIA. The equations, per-family values and sources are on GPU power model.
Workload boundness Each job carries cpuUtilization, gpuUtilization, memoryIntensity, ioIntensity and cpuFeedIntensityGpu, rather than a single label. Memory and IO intensity soften the slowdown a CPU cap or DVFS causes. A GPU job with a high CPU feed intensity also slows when the CPU is throttled.
Heterogeneous caps The controller manager writes caps as percentages by default (CPU of its cap range, GPU of the per-device maximum), and the agent or the simulator resolves them into watts from the node’s own hardware data. Absolute per-device caps remain possible for deterministic experiments.
What the simulator exports Node CPU and GPU power (averaged and instantaneous), per-GPU caps, power and temperature, thermal-throttle fractions, performance multipliers, integrated energy and job completion statistics. See Power Simulator.
6.8 Emulated nodes: governor and clock physics An emulated node (emulate mode) runs the CPU and GPU governors its profile describes; the other modes keep an implied performance governor.
CPU. Each cpufreq policy’s governor sets a frequency every 100 ms substep, following the Linux v6.12 rules (phys.GovernorStep); powersave under intel_pstate with HWP and amd-pstate-epp follows an assumed EPP-shaped curve. Slower clocks keep the CPU busy longer for the same work, and a binding RAPL or HSMP cap wins over every governor. GPU. The cap and the governor are two limits on one clock: the GPU runs at the lower of the two, never at their product (phys.GPUPowerWithClock, phys.GPUThroughputWithClock). Parameters. Every value is assumed and to be calibrated. The rules per governor are on Governors; the GPU clock rules and parameters on GPU power model.
Preset names The emulator names the preset a CPU package or a GPU runs (the joulie.hw.governor.preset attribute of its metrics) with the reverse mapping of pkg/governor (ReverseCPU, ReverseAMD, ReverseNvidia): the name is the preset whose plan the agent would write for that state. A state that no preset, or more than one, maps to has no name, and a GPU without a mapping table reports none. The tie-breaking rules are on Governors.
Peer transfers GPU to GPU copies share each receiver’s gpus.transfer.peerLinkGBps. A family can have a receiver gate (gpus.transfer.receiverGate): a receiver whose data path is at its lowest level, or idle under auto, lets through only a fraction of the link. The gate is off in every builtin profile; SIM_GPU_RECEIVER_GATE=on turns it on for what-if runs. Details are on GPU power model.
6.9 Governor presets A frequency governor is a control dimension of its own, next to the power cap: the cap bounds the power, the governor chooses the frequency below that bound. Joulie writes one vendor-neutral preset per component in NodeTwin.spec, and pkg/governor is the only place a preset becomes a native setting. The mapping is per driver in CPU support and per GPU family in GPU support.
Component Preset Intent CPU performance highest frequency within scaling_max_freq at any load: race to idle CPU balanced demand-driven, quick ramp CPU efficiency demand-driven with an energy bias CPU boost on or off frequency boost (turbo), changed only when the spec names it GPU auto the vendor default GPU sustained data-path clocks (memory, fabric) at their maximum, idle gating kept, the compute clock free to idle GPU efficient the compute clock under a ceiling, computeClockCeilingPctOfMax of its maximum (80 % by default), the data path dynamic GPU low every clock at its minimum; for experiments GPU peak every clock at its maximum, idle gating off on AMD; for experiments Off by default. It needs both the controller manager’s GOVERNOR_CONTROL and the agent’s GOVERNOR_WRITES; discovery is always on. Restored. The agent records the state it found before its first write and restores it when a preset disappears, when writes are turned off, and on exit (Governor control). GPU nodes. A GPU node gets no CPU governor unless CPU_GOVERNOR_ON_GPU_NODES is true. sustained. No default selects it; opt a GPU model in once a measurement shows the gain. Policy. The agent is Joulie’s node-side component: it discovers the node’s hardware and applies the caps and governor presets the controller manager plans. It does not plan policy.
Responsibilities Every reconcile (RECONCILE_INTERVAL, 20 s), for each node it owns, the agent:
Step What 1 discovers CPU and GPU hardware, cap ranges and governors 2 publishes them as NodeHardware 3 reads the desired state in NodeTwin.spec 4 applies the governor presets and the CPU and GPU caps, through host interfaces or HTTP 5 reports the outcome in NodeTwin.status.controlStatus and on /metrics Inputs and outputs Inputs Outputs NodeTwin.spec: profile, caps, governor presets NodeHardware: discovered hardware and capabilities backend variables (TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE, TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL, TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL; default host) writes to RAPL, cpufreq and GPU interfaces, or the simulator over HTTP node labels (hardware identity, NFD and GPU feature discovery) NodeTwin.status.controlStatus: applied, blocked, error or none per component Prometheus metrics on /metrics (Metrics Reference) NodeHardware is the agent’s output; you do not write it.
Runtime modes daemonset: one agent pod per managed real node, for real hardware. pool: a few agent pods share many logical nodes (sharded), for KWOK and simulator runs. Both select nodes with joulie.io/managed=true. Setup is in Agent Runtime Modes.
Governor discovery Every reconcile the agent reads the CPU and GPU frequency governors under the host /sys (mounted at /host-sys), and for NVIDIA through nvidia-smi, without writing anything. It publishes them in NodeHardware.status.cpu.governor, status.cpu.landmarks and status.gpu.governor: the driver, the current state, the presets the node accepts, whether it is writable, and the baseline a restore puts back. Discovery is always on.
kubectl get nodehardware <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.cpu.governor.presets}' Governor control The agent writes governor presets only with GOVERNOR_WRITES=true (Agent governor control). It maps each preset to the node’s native settings, writes them, reads them back where it can, and reports the outcome in status.controlStatus.cpuGovernor and gpuGovernor, with the native setting in applied.
Result Meaning applied, equivalent in force; checked again every reconcile applied-unverified NVIDIA clock locks issued, not yet seen in use unsupported, not-applied the node cannot take the preset, or the write did not hold; retried after 30 min or when the intent changes refused permission denied; not retried until the agent restarts drift, contended another writer changed the setting; re-applied, then left alone after the third drift in 30 min disabled GOVERNOR_WRITES=false or SIMULATE_ONLY restored the preset left the spec and the baseline went back error the mechanism could not run (missing tool); retried after 5 min When a preset leaves the spec, or the agent stops with GOVERNOR_RESTORE_ON_EXIT=true (default), the agent puts back the baseline it recorded before its first write. What each preset becomes per driver is in CPU support and GPU support.
CPU enforcement algorithm Take packagePowerCapWatts, or resolve packagePowerCapPctOfMax to watts against the node’s RAPL range (for an HTTP backend, the hardware catalog’s range for the node’s CPU). Write the watts to RAPL (host files, or rapl.set_power_cap_watts over HTTP). Without RAPL, fall back to DVFS: a feedback loop on scaling_max_freq that holds the measured power under the cap. A percentage with no range to resolve it becomes a throttle percentage directly (dvfs.set_throttle_pct over HTTP). The tuning variables are under Agent DVFS control. The backend in use is joulie_backend_mode{mode=none|rapl|dvfs}, and the log line resolved cpu cap from pct names the range used.
GPU power cap The agent resolves spec.gpu.powerCap to watts per GPU and writes the same cap to every GPU of the node, skipping GPUs already at it, and reads the result back where the driver allows.
Vendor Mechanism Needs NVIDIA nvidia-smi -pl, per GPU nvidia-smi in the agent (Agent GPU tools) AMD power1_cap of the amdgpu hwmon device, no tool root agent, writable /host-sys (the chart’s default) Intel power1_max or power2_max of the i915 or xe hwmon device, discrete GPUs only as AMD A node whose GPUs have no settable limit reports blocked; a failed write is error naming the GPU, while the other GPUs are still capped. Check a node with:
kubectl get nodetwin <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.controlStatus.gpu}' Performance -> eco transition and safeguards The controller manager decides when a node may drop to eco; the agent only enforces the published target. A node planned for eco that still runs performance pods stays draining with its performance caps until they finish, so they are never throttled mid-run, and nothing is evicted. See the node state model and Policy Algorithms.

body:
The digital twin turns each node’s measured power and hardware limits into a few scores the scheduler and the policy use. It is a closed-form model in the controller manager (pkg/controller/twin), computed every reconcile, and its output is NodeTwin.status.
What the digital twin computes Field in NodeTwin.status Meaning Range Read by predictedPowerHeadroomScore share of the node’s capped power budget still unused up to 100, negative when over budget scheduler (fallback) predictedCoolingStressScore measured power over node TDP, scaled up in warm ambient air 0 to 100 scheduler predictedPsuStressScore rack (or cluster) power over a 50 kW reference capacity 0 to 100 nobody yet estimatedPUE cooling stress restated on a PUE scale 1.05 to 1.40 nobody yet schedulableClass performance, eco or draining scheduler, controller manager powerMeasurement measured power, TDP, capped budget and trend, per node watts scheduler conditions AgentReporting: whether an agent enforces the caps the Agent column of kubectl get nodetwins Every power score starts from the measured node power powerMeasurement.measuredNodePowerW, not from the caps.
kubectl get nodetwin <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.powerMeasurement}' Where the power reading comes from NODE_POWER_SOURCE on the controller manager selects it, and powerMeasurement.source says which one answered:
NODE_POWER_SOURCE Reads source on failure prometheus (chart default) one query per reconcile: hw.energy and hw.power of the CPU packages and GPUs (Input metrics (OpenTelemetry)), or Kepler with NODE_POWER_PRESET prometheus-no-data http NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT, one OTLP JSON document per node (the simulator) http-error, http-no-endpoint static (code default) nothing: 0 W, so every node reads headroom 100 and stress 0 NODE_POWER_SCOPE=components (default) covers the CPU packages and GPUs, the same boundary as the TDP; host reads the whole host. Configure a source before treating the scores as a ranking signal.
Node TDP and the capped budget The twin derives two budgets from NodeHardware: the node TDP (CPU max watts per socket times sockets, plus GPU max watts times GPU power domains) and the capped budget (the same with the caps of NodeTwin.spec applied). A GPU cap counts only where it applies (not when the agent reports it blocked or error), and the CPU budget never goes below the bottom of the CPU cap range. Both appear in powerMeasurement as nodeTdpW and nodeCappedPowerW.
Cooling stress Measured power over node TDP, times an ambient multiplier that is 1 at 20 °C or with no reading and rises to 2 at 45 °C. Facility metrics are off by default (ENABLE_FACILITY_METRICS=false), so the multiplier is usually 1; with them on, the twin uses the node’s inlet temperature, then its cooling zone’s, then the outdoor one (Facility metrics).
PSU stress and estimated PUE PSU stress is per rack when nodes carry joulie.io/rack and cluster-wide otherwise; it is 0 on a default install. Estimated PUE is 1.05 plus 0.35 times cooling stress over 100. Neither enters the scheduler’s score.
How it feeds the scheduler The scheduler extender caches NodeTwin (30 s) and uses schedulableClass to filter and powerMeasurement plus cooling stress to score (Scheduler Extender).
How it feeds the controller manager schedulableClass is draining while a node moving from performance to eco still runs performance pods. The twin reads no governor field (Governor policy).

A policy decides how many managed nodes run the performance profile; every other node runs eco. Pick one with POLICY_TYPE on the controller manager. The policies are in pkg/controller/policy/.
Demand is the number of pods annotated joulie.io/workload-class: performance; pods without the annotation are standard.
Which performance nodes static_partition and queue_aware_v1 compute a count; the controller manager then splits it across hardware families (gpu:<model>, cpu:<model>) in proportion to family size, at least one node per family, keeping nodes already in performance first. A change of one in the count moves exactly one node. The split is exported as joulie_policy_family_nodes{family} and joulie_policy_family_performance_nodes{family}.
static_partition The default. Use it for a fixed, predictable share of performance nodes: about STATIC_HP_FRAC of every family.
Knob Default Meaning STATIC_HP_FRAC 0.50 fraction of nodes in performance: round(N * STATIC_HP_FRAC) Exercised in the CPU-Only Benchmark and the Heterogeneous GPU Cluster Benchmark.
queue_aware_v1 Use it when performance demand varies: the count grows with the performance pods that are running or pending.
Knob Default Meaning QUEUE_HP_BASE_FRAC 0.60 base fraction of nodes in performance QUEUE_PERF_PER_HP_NODE 10 performance pods one performance node absorbs QUEUE_HP_MIN 1 lower bound of the count QUEUE_HP_MAX 1000000 upper bound of the count The count is max(round(N * QUEUE_HP_BASE_FRAC), ceil(P / QUEUE_PERF_PER_HP_NODE)), clamped to [QUEUE_HP_MIN, QUEUE_HP_MAX], with P the running and pending performance pods. Exercised in the same two benchmarks.
rule_swap_v1 (debug policy) For debugging only: it alternates which of the first two nodes, by name, is eco every RECONCILE_INTERVAL, so transitions are visible. It has no knobs.
Downgrade Guard A node planned for eco that still runs performance pods becomes draining: it keeps its performance caps, and the scheduler extender sends no new performance pods to it. When those pods finish it gets the eco caps. Nothing is evicted.

body:
Joulie’s scheduler extender keeps performance pods off eco nodes and ranks the remaining nodes by power headroom and cooling stress. It is an HTTP extender that kube-scheduler calls; it does not replace kube-scheduler. The chart always deploys it; without it pods get standard Kubernetes scheduling.
How a pod gets scheduled (end-to-end) kube-scheduler picks up the new pod and runs its own filters (resources, taints, affinity). It calls Joulie’s POST /filter: performance pods lose the eco and draining nodes. It calls POST /prioritize: Joulie scores each remaining node 0 to 100 for this pod and returns it as a 0 to 10 priority. kube-scheduler adds Joulie’s priority, times the extender weight, to its own plugin scores and binds the pod to the best node. Placement intent comes from one pod annotation, joulie.io/workload-class, so users write no scheduling rules. The extender does not migrate or evict pods and never overrides resource fits.
What the extender reads Source What it provides Cache NodeTwin.status schedulableClass, cooling stress, headroom, powerMeasurement (measured, capped, TDP, trend) CACHE_TTL (30 s) NodeHardware.status CPU cores and max watts, GPU count and max watts CACHE_TTL the pod joulie.io/workload-class, CPU and GPU requests per request Filter logic Pod Node Result joulie.io/workload-class: performance schedulableClass eco or draining (or label joulie.io/power-profile: eco without a twin) rejected performance any other node, or no NodeTwin allowed standard (no annotation, or standard) any node allowed Score logic The score is pod-specific: the extender estimates the watts this pod would add to each node from its CPU and GPU requests (GPU shares for MIG devices and partitions, see Shared and partitioned GPUs), adds them to the node’s measured power, and compares the result with the node’s capped budget. Nodes with room left after the pod score high; heavy pods on nearly full nodes and eco nodes, whose budget is lower, score low.
score = headroomScore*0.7 + (100-coolingStress)*0.15 + trendBonus + profileBonus + pressureRelief Term Range From projected headroom x 0.7 negative to 70 powerMeasurement.measuredNodePowerW plus the pod’s watts, against nodeCappedPowerW (Digital Twin) (100 - cooling stress) x 0.15 0 to 15 predictedCoolingStressScore trend bonus -25 to 25 powerTrendWPerMin: falling power scores higher profile bonus 0 or 10 +10 for a standard pod on an eco node pressure relief -30 to 0 a standard pod on a performance node, when performance nodes are congested The score is clamped to 0 to 100. A node with stale (older than TWIN_STALENESS_THRESHOLD) or missing twin data gets a neutral 50. PSU stress and estimated PUE are not part of the score.
Environment variables Variable Default Purpose EXTENDER_ADDR :9876 HTTP listen address CACHE_TTL 30s Minimum interval between rebuilding the scoring maps from the informer cache TWIN_STALENESS_THRESHOLD 5m Max age of NodeTwin data before treating as stale MARGINAL_CPU_UTIL_COEFF (from powerest.DefaultCoefficients) CPU marginal power coefficient MARGINAL_GPU_UTIL_COEFF_STANDARD (from powerest.DefaultCoefficients) GPU marginal power coefficient for standard pods MARGINAL_GPU_UTIL_COEFF_PERFORMANCE (from powerest.DefaultCoefficients) GPU marginal power coefficient for performance pods Debug endpoint GET /debug/scoring returns the current scoring state of every node as JSON, without a scheduling event:
{ "coefficients": {"cpuUtilCoeff": 0.8, "gpuUtilCoeffStandard": 0.6, "gpuUtilCoeffPerformance": 0.9}, "nodes": [ { "nodeName": "node-0", "schedulableClass": "performance", "headroom": 72.5, "coolingStress": 31.3, "measuredPowerW": 450.0, "cappedPowerW": 1200.0, "nodeTdpW": 2000.0, "powerTrendWPerMin": -5.2, "baseScore": 60.0, "cpuTotalCores": 128, "cpuMaxWattsTotal": 700.0, "gpuCount": 8, "gpuMaxWattsPerGpu": 400.0, "hasGpu": true, "stale": false } ] } How to deploy The scheduler extender is deployed as part of the Joulie Helm chart.
KubeSchedulerConfiguration extender block apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1 kind: KubeSchedulerConfiguration profiles: - schedulerName: default-scheduler extenders: - urlPrefix: "http://joulie-scheduler-extender.joulie-system.svc.cluster.local:9876" filterVerb: "filter" prioritizeVerb: "prioritize" weight: 1 enableHTTPS: false nodeCacheCapable: false ignorable: true ignorable: true lets the scheduler proceed normally if the extender is temporarily unreachable.
Testing The extender exposes /healthz. To check filter decisions without a running scheduler:
curl -s -X POST \ http://localhost:9876/filter \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"pod": {...}, "nodes": {"items": [...]}}' What to read next Digital Twin Pod Compatibility Joulie Controller Manager The full scoring formula, the marginal power model and its default coefficients, the fallbacks and worked examples: Scheduler scoring on the wiki.

This page follows one placement decision from the hardware counters to the chosen node. Each stage is a separate component that hands its result to the next through Prometheus or a CRD, and each links to the page that documents it.
End-to-end pipeline RAPL/NVML readings as OpenTelemetry metrics (or Kepler) -> Prometheus (OTLP receiver, or scrape) -> Digital twin (NodeTwin.status) -> Scheduler extender (filter + score) -> Placement decision Stage 1: Telemetry collection CPU (RAPL) and GPU (NVML, ROCm SMI) power reach Prometheus as the OpenTelemetry metrics hw.energy and hw.power, or through Kepler: Input metrics (OpenTelemetry).
Stage 2: Prometheus aggregation The controller manager runs one grouped query per input every reconcile, over a rate() window of PROMETHEUS_RATE_WINDOW (5 min): Prometheus settings.
Stage 3: Digital twin computation The twin turns measured power and NodeHardware into headroom, cooling stress and PSU stress per node in NodeTwin.status: Digital Twin.
Stage 4: Scheduler filter and scoring The extender keeps performance pods off eco and draining nodes, then scores each node by the headroom left after this pod’s estimated watts, cooling stress and power trend: Scheduler Extender.
Stage 5: Placement kube-scheduler adds the extender’s priority to its own scores and binds the pod; resource fits stay Kubernetes’ own: Pod Compatibility.
Facility signals Cooling stress is the score’s only facility term: a node near its cooling limit loses up to 15 points even with spare headroom. The extender does not weight power by PUE, and PSU stress is computed but not scored yet.
Scoring Formula Validation tests the formula at scale; its results do not stand yet, and it is being redone.
What to read next Scheduler Extender Digital Twin The research this design builds on, with citations, and what Joulie adds: Related work on the wiki; the scoring detail is on Scheduler scoring.

Complete reference for all Joulie environment variables. These are set via Helm values or directly in the Deployment/DaemonSet manifests.
Defaults listed below are the code defaults. The Helm chart (charts/joulie/values.yaml) overrides some of them: notably, the controller manager NODE_SELECTOR defaults to joulie.io/managed=true in the chart even though the code default is node-role.kubernetes.io/worker.
Booleans. The agent, the controller manager and the simulator read every on/off variable the same way: true, 1, yes or on, and false, 0, no or off, in any case, with surrounding spaces ignored. Unset or empty means the default. Any other value keeps the default and logs one warning naming the variable, so a typo never flips a switch. The exceptions are SIM_OTEL_FILE_METRICS, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED and fakesmi’s HWEMU_UNPRIVILEGED, whose rows say how they are read.
Images The image tag values (agent.image.tag, controllerManager.image.tag, schedulerExtender.image.tag, and image.tag in the simulator chart) default to empty, which pulls the chart’s appVersion: a released chart runs its release’s images, a chart from a checkout (appVersion: latest) the newest stable release. Every image is a multi-arch index of linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
Details: Configuration notes, Images.
Agent Variable Default Description AGENT_MODE daemonset daemonset (one agent per node) or pool (shared agents with sharding) NODE_NAME (required in daemonset mode) Name of the node this agent manages RECONCILE_INTERVAL 20s How often the agent reconciles desired state METRICS_ADDR :8080 Address for the Prometheus metrics endpoint SPEC_READ_TIMEOUT 5m How long the agent tolerates failed reads of its NodeTwin spec before it relaxes every cap and puts the governor baseline back, until a read succeeds. A Go duration such as 90s; a value it cannot parse keeps 5m SIMULATE_ONLY false If true, agent discovers hardware but does not apply power caps or governors (governor result disabled) HARDWARE_CATALOG_PATH (empty: the catalog embedded in the binary) Path to a hardware inventory catalog YAML that replaces the embedded one KUBE_CLIENT_QPS 50 Queries per second the agent’s Kubernetes client may send KUBE_CLIENT_BURST 100 Burst above KUBE_CLIENT_QPS the agent’s Kubernetes client may send Agent pool mode Variable Default Description POOL_NODE_SELECTOR joulie.io/managed=true Label selector for nodes managed by pool agents POOL_SHARDS 1 Total number of shards for pool mode partitioning POOL_SHARD_ID (from pod ordinal) Shard ID for this agent instance Agent DVFS control Variable Default Description DVFS_EMA_ALPHA 0.3 Exponential moving average smoothing factor for power tracking DVFS_HIGH_MARGIN_W 10.0 Power above cap (watts) to trigger frequency reduction DVFS_LOW_MARGIN_W 15.0 Power below cap (watts) to trigger frequency increase DVFS_STEP_PCT 10 Frequency throttle step size (%) DVFS_COOLDOWN 20s Minimum duration between DVFS adjustments DVFS_TRIP_COUNT 2 Consecutive samples outside margin before acting DVFS_MIN_FREQ_KHZ 1500000 Floor frequency for DVFS throttling (kHz) Agent governor control The agent always publishes its node’s CPU and GPU governors in NodeHardware (Governor discovery). It writes the presets of its NodeTwin only with GOVERNOR_WRITES true, and the controller manager sets them only with GOVERNOR_CONTROL on (Governor control).
Variable Default Chart Description GOVERNOR_WRITES false false Write the governor presets. false writes none and reports disabled, but still puts back, once, the settings an earlier run changed (result restored). GOVERNOR_RESTORE_ON_EXIT true true On SIGTERM or SIGINT, put the baseline back before the agent exits. SIGKILL and OOM kills restore nothing. Writes need the agent’s /host-sys mount, root user and privileges, as the chart gives; without them the result is refused (NodeHardware writable: false). NVIDIA presets need nvidia-smi in the agent (Agent GPU tools); without it the result is error. HTTP control mode and pool mode write no governor (unsupported). What each preset becomes per CPU driver and GPU family: CPU support, GPU support. Results, retries and restores: Governor control. Check them with: kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,CPU-GOV:.status.controlStatus.cpuGovernor.result,CPU-NATIVE:.status.controlStatus.cpuGovernor.applied,GPU-GOV:.status.controlStatus.gpuGovernor.result,GPU-NATIVE:.status.controlStatus.gpuGovernor.applied Details: Configuration notes, Agent governor control.
Agent telemetry and control backends Variable Default Description TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE host CPU telemetry source: host (the node’s RAPL files), http (TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT), none TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL host CPU control backend: host, http, none TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL host GPU control backend: host, http, none TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) HTTP endpoint for CPU telemetry, {node} replaced with the node name (e.g., http://sim:18080/otlp/telemetry/{node}), answering OTLP JSON (HTTP input format). The legacy packagePowerWatts JSON is read with a warning until v0.4.0. An answer over 8 MiB is an error. TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) HTTP endpoint for CPU control (e.g., http://sim:18080/control/{node}) TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL_MODE (empty) With TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL=http: dvfs sends throttle percentages (dvfs.set_throttle_pct) and runs the DVFS loop for a cap in watts; any other value sends caps in watts (rapl.set_power_cap_watts) (CPU enforcement algorithm). TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL_HTTP_ENDPOINT (empty) HTTP endpoint for GPU control (e.g., http://sim:18080/control/{node}) TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL_MODE (empty) GPU control mode override TELEMETRY_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 2 HTTP client timeout for telemetry/control requests, in whole seconds Details: Configuration notes, Agent telemetry and control backends.
Agent chart values Helm values of charts/joulie that shape the agent pods. agent.tolerations, agent.runtimeClassName and the agent.extra* hooks apply to the DaemonSet and the emulated agents, not to the pool StatefulSet.
Value Default Effect agent.mode daemonset daemonset (one agent per node matching agent.daemonset.nodeSelector), pool, emulated or none (Agent Runtime Modes). agent.tolerations - operator: Exists (every taint) Tolerations of the agent pods. The default tolerates every taint, so agent.daemonset.nodeSelector alone decides where the agent runs. A list replaces the default, and [] tolerates none. A managed node the agent does not reach is planned but not enforced (Managed nodes without an agent). agent.runtimeClassName "" RuntimeClass of the agent pods, for example the one of the NVIDIA container runtime, which puts the node’s driver tools into the container. agent.extraEnv [] EnvVar entries added after the chart’s own. agent.extraVolumes [] Volume entries added after the chart’s own. agent.extraVolumeMounts [] VolumeMount entries added to the agent container after the chart’s own. agent.emulated.root /var/lib/joulie-hwemu The simulator’s SIM_HWEMU_ROOT, from which each emulated agent mounts its node’s tree (sys at /host-sys, cpuinfo over /proc/cpuinfo, state, bin and lib under /emu). agent.emulated.hostNodeSelector joulie.io/hwemu-host: "true" Node selector of the emulated agents: the node that holds the trees and runs the simulator. agent.emulated.path /emu/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin PATH of the emulated agents, so the emulated GPU tools come first. agent.emulated.fuse false Mount sys and state from the simulator’s FUSE views, for a simulator with emulate.fuse. The DaemonSet ignores it. agent.emulated.nodes [] One entry per emulated node, as simcluster agents writes them: name (the Node, also the literal NODE_NAME), profile, devNvidiactl, extraVolumes, extraVolumeMounts. Entry i becomes the Deployment joulie-agent-emu-<i>. A name that is not a Node name, or is listed twice, fails the render. Emulated agents are what the simulated cluster runs. Details: Configuration notes, Agent chart values.
Agent GPU tools The agent reads and caps NVIDIA GPUs by running nvidia-smi from its PATH. AMD and Intel GPUs need no tool, only the chart’s root agent and writable /host-sys: the agent writes the amdgpu power1_cap files, or the i915 or xe power1_max or power2_max files, with backend host-intel (Agent host backends).
The agent image ships no GPU tool and no C library: bring the driver’s tools and libraries in with agent.runtimeClassName (such as the NVIDIA container runtime), or with agent.extraVolumes, agent.extraVolumeMounts and agent.extraEnv. No recipe has been verified on a real NVIDIA node yet, so after installing check every GPU node:
kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,GPU:.status.controlStatus.gpu.result,MESSAGE:.status.controlStatus.gpu.message A tool that cannot run shows error with a message starting gpu inventory failed, or blocked with no supported GPU backend detected; the GPUs then keep their limits. Details: Configuration notes, Agent GPU tools.
Managed nodes without an agent The controller manager plans every managed node, agent or not. The NodeTwin condition AgentReporting (the Agent column of kubectl get nodetwins) is True while an agent publishes the node’s NodeHardware, and False (NoNodeHardware, or NodeHardwareStale after 15 minutes without a write) when the caps are planned but not enforced. joulie_twin_nodes_agent_reporting counts the nodes per status and reason (Twin agent coverage). Usual causes: a taint the agent does not tolerate, a node outside agent.daemonset.nodeSelector, or an image without the node’s platform.
kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns='NODE:.spec.nodeName,AGENT:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="AgentReporting")].status,REASON:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="AgentReporting")].reason' Details: Configuration notes, Agent.

Governor control Off by default. With GOVERNOR_CONTROL on, the controller manager writes a vendor-neutral governor preset into each managed node’s NodeTwin (spec.cpu.governor, spec.gpu.governor) by the profile it runs at, and the agent maps it to native settings once it runs with GOVERNOR_WRITES true. Which node gets which preset: Governor policy.
Variable Default Description GOVERNOR_CONTROL off off, cpu (CPU governors only), gpu (GPU governors only) or all. CPU_GOVERNOR_PERFORMANCE_PRESET performance CPU preset of performance nodes: performance (highest frequency at any load), balanced (demand-driven, quick ramp) or efficiency (demand-driven with an energy bias). CPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_PRESET efficiency CPU preset of eco nodes. Provisional: it does not pass the simulator’s governor exploration as a default for every CPU driver, and it lengthens compute-bound bursts. CPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_BOOST empty on or off: frequency boost (turbo) with the eco preset, on nodes whose agent found a boost control (status.cpu.governor.boost). Empty leaves boost alone. CPU_GOVERNOR_ON_GPU_NODES false Write the CPU governor on GPU nodes too. GPU_GOVERNOR_PERFORMANCE_PRESET empty GPU preset of performance nodes: auto, sustained, efficient, low, peak, or empty for none. GPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_PRESET efficient GPU preset of eco nodes; set it to an empty value to write none. GPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_CEILING_PCT_OF_MAX 80 Compute clock ceiling of the efficient preset, in percent of the GPU’s maximum compute clock, in (0, 100]. Written only with efficient; a value out of range gives 80. Provisional (governor exploration). GPU_GOVERNOR_MODEL_PRESETS_JSON {} Presets per GPU model: {"<model>": {"performance": "<preset>", "eco": "<preset>", "ecoCeilingPctOfMax": <pct>}}, keyed like GPU_MODEL_CAPS_JSON. A field left out keeps the default, "" writes none for that model, and an invalid field is dropped with a warning. GPU_GOVERNOR_SUSTAINED_ONLY_MULTI_GPU false If true, a node whose GPU preset is sustained gets it only while a running pod on it requests 2 or more GPUs (units of any GPU resource: whole GPUs, MIG devices, partitions, shared replicas), and no GPU governor otherwise. GPU presets: auto is the vendor default; sustained holds memory and fabric clocks at their maximum (no default selects it); efficient caps the compute clock at the ceiling; low and peak are for experiments. All defaults are provisional until measured. Meanings: Hardware modeling; which node gets which: Governor policy.
The overview dashboard’s “Agent: Governors” row plots the presets in effect (joulie_agent_governor_state) and the writes per result (joulie_agent_governor_writes_total). Details: Configuration notes, Governor control.
Facility metrics The facility poller reads seven inputs from Prometheus each poll: outdoor ambient temperature, IT power and cooling power, the per-zone, per-rack and per-node inputs (Node topology), and the grid carbon intensity when its query is set. An input whose query fails or returns nothing is unknown until a later poll reads it. Metrics: joulie_twin_input_queries_total{input,result}, joulie_twin_facility_* and joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_grams_per_kW_h (Metrics).

FACILITY_IT_POWER_QUERY from the preset unset Power of the IT equipment, one value in watts. FACILITY_COOLING_POWER_QUERY from the preset unset Power of the cooling, one value in watts. FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_UNIT gCO2eq/kWh unset Unit of the carbon intensity value: a mass (g, kg, t, lb, lbs), optionally followed by CO2, CO2e or CO2eq, over kWh or MWh, in any case, such as lbsCO2/MWh. Any other unit stops the controller manager at start while the query is set. Required with the query: the controller manager does not start without it. A query variable replaces its input’s query under any preset. Details: Configuration notes, Facility metrics.
Grid carbon intensity Joulie ships no carbon intensity provider. If you already export one to Prometheus, point FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_QUERY at it, with ENABLE_FACILITY_METRICS=true, and say what the value is:
controllerManager: env: ENABLE_FACILITY_METRICS: "true" FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_QUERY: 'watttime_co2_moer{region="CAISO_NORTH"}' FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_UNIT: "lbsCO2/MWh" FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_SIGNAL: "marginal" The query must return one series, so select the cluster’s grid zone with a label matcher. The value is converted to gCO2eq/kWh and exported as joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_grams_per_kW_h{joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_signal}; no policy acts on it yet. Details: Configuration notes, Grid carbon intensity.
Deprecated aliases, removed in v0.4.0: FACILITY_AMBIENT_TEMP_METRIC, FACILITY_IT_POWER_METRIC, FACILITY_COOLING_POWER_METRIC, the former names of the first three query variables. They are read only when the new name is unset, with a warning naming the replacement, and the bare metric name they hold keeps its meaning.
Node topology Optional node labels give per-rack PSU stress and per-zone cooling stress:
joulie.io/rack: physical rack identifier (e.g., rack-1) joulie.io/cooling-zone: cooling zone identifier (e.g., zone-a) With them, PSU stress is computed per rack: the rack power input (FACILITY_RACK_POWER_QUERY) when it reads that rack, otherwise the sum of the estimated power of the rack’s nodes. A twin’s ambient temperature is the most local one known: the node’s inlet (FACILITY_NODE_INLET_TEMP_QUERY), then its cooling zone’s (FACILITY_ZONE_AMBIENT_TEMP_QUERY), then the outdoor ambient.
Nodes without the labels use cluster-wide stress, and still their inlet temperature when the facility reads one.

Simulator This section covers the binaries under simulator/cmd. Each subsection names the binary that reads its variables. The simulator’s modes are described in Simulator.
Simulator basics The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) reads these in every mode.

Simulator power limits The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) reads these at startup. For a node the hardware catalogue matches, an unset variable leaves the field to the catalogue; the built-in default applies only to hardware it does not know. A node class key (in parentheses) wins over both, and 0 or less counts as unset (wiki: CPU power model, Where the numbers come from).
Variable Default Description SIM_P_MAX_W sockets x catalogue TDP, else 420 Peak CPU power of the generic model, at full load and full frequency (pMaxW). A node with a measured curve uses the curve instead. SIM_BETA_FREQ 1.43 Exponent of the frequency scale in the CPU’s dynamic power, on the generic model and on a measured curve: P = P(0) + (P(u) - P(0)) x f^beta. Its fit is on the wiki’s CPU power model. SIM_RAPL_CAP_MIN_W 0 Lowest node CPU cap the simulator accepts; a cap below it is refused with an error. 0 is no floor; a cap the CPU cannot reach holds it at its lowest-frequency power. SIM_CPU_SOCKET_CAP_MAX_W catalogue TDP, else 400 Upper end of the per-socket CPU cap: the node cap is split evenly over the sockets and clamped to this range (cpuSocketCapMaxW). SIM_GPU_MAX_WATTS_PER_GPU catalogue maxBoardPowerW, else 300 Board power of one GPU at full load, and its highest cap (gpu.maxWattsPerGpu). SIM_GPU_MIN_CAP_WATTS_PER_GPU catalogue minBoardPowerW, else half the maximum, else 80 Lowest cap of one GPU (gpu.minCapWattsPerGpu); a cap below it is refused with an error. A catalogue minimum above a maximum set by a class or a variable is lowered to that maximum. A measured two-socket curve from the catalogue is scaled by sockets/2 on a node with another socket count.

Simulator physics step Outside the emulate-mode cluster spec, the simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) advances a node’s model only in a physics step, in simulated time, split into equal substeps (Power Simulator).
Variable Default Description SIM_POLL_INTERVAL 15s (chart: 8s) Kubernetes mode: how often the simulator lists pods and nodes. A value of 0 or less logs a warning and takes 15s. SIM_PHYSICS_TICK 1s Kubernetes mode without emulate mode: every modelled node is stepped by the wall time since the last tick, in substeps of at most 100 ms. A value of 0 or less logs a warning and takes 1s. In emulate mode SIM_EMULATE_TICK steps them instead, and standalone mode steps them on its own tick. SIM_SA_SUBSTEP SIM_SA_DT Standalone mode: the longest physics substep, in simulated seconds; each SIM_SA_DT tick is split into equal substeps no longer than this. Shorter follows the cap, frequency and thermal lags more closely, at the cost of run time. Simulator hardware emulation fakesmi (simulator/cmd/fakesmi) stands in for nvidia-smi, rocm-smi and amd-smi on an emulated node. It runs as the tool its name says, through a bin/<tool> link, and reads and writes the node’s emulated hardware files instead of a driver. The agent does not read these variables; only fakesmi does.
Variable Default Description HWEMU_SYS_ROOT /host-sys The emulated node’s sys/ directory, where the amdgpu PCI and hwmon attributes live. The default is where an emulated agent pod mounts it. HWEMU_STATE_ROOT /emu/state The emulated node’s state/ directory, with tools.json (the tools the node has) and the GPU state. The default is where an emulated agent pod mounts it. HWEMU_ROOTFS / The file system the real tool would run in, where fakesmi looks for what the tool needs before it runs (below). The default is the agent container’s own root. HWEMU_UNPRIVILEGED false Run the tools as a user without root would: 1, true or another word Go’s strconv.ParseBool reads as true; anything else, unset included, means root. Sets then fail or do nothing, as the real tools do without root (nvidia-smi -pl exits 4 with Insufficient Permissions); reads work. A tool that tools.json does not list exits 127 with fakesmi: <tool> is not installed on this emulated node.
A listed tool first checks, under HWEMU_ROOTFS, that the files the real tool needs exist (the ELF loader, the C libraries and NVML for nvidia-smi, python3 for rocm-smi and amd-smi), and fails with the real tool’s exit code and message when one is missing. Details: Configuration notes, Simulator hardware emulation.
Simulator emulate mode In emulate mode the simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) emulates the bare-metal nodes a cluster spec lists, with a sysfs tree, /proc/cpuinfo and GPU tool state per node under SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/<node>/ that an unmodified agent caps as a real node. /control/<node> answers 409 for an emulated node. See Emulate Mode.
Variable Default Description SIM_EMULATE false Turn emulate mode on. Refused with SIM_STANDALONE, with an empty SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC, and with SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL=legacy, since a legacy trace cannot drive emulated nodes. SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC (empty) Path of the cluster spec, a sim.joulie.io/v1alpha1 ClusterSpec such as tests/simcluster/specs/smoke.yaml: each node, its hardware profile, pool, rack and cooling zone, and the facility. SIM_HWEMU_ROOT /var/lib/joulie-hwemu Directory of the emulated trees, one <node>/ per spec node. One simulator holds it at a time; a second one fails to start. SIM_HWEMU_FUSE false Serve each spec node’s sys and state through FUSE at SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/fuse/<node>/, so writes and counters behave as the kernel’s do (FUSE mode). Needs /dev/fuse, and as root CAP_SYS_ADMIN; another user needs fusermount3. SIM_EMULATE_TICK 1s Physics tick: every spec node advances to wall time once per tick; a late tick is caught up by the next. The nodes outside the spec are stepped on the same tick (see “Simulator physics step”). SIM_GPU_RECEIVER_GATE profile Whether the receiver gate of peer transfers applies: profile (each profile’s gpus.transfer.receiverGate.enabled, off in every builtin profile), off everywhere, or on on every GPU profile, for what-if runs. Any other value logs a warning and takes profile (peer transfers). SIM_EMULATE_WORKERS 0 Nodes stepped in parallel; 0 means GOMAXPROCS, at most 12 (Tick cost); a set value is used as given. SIM_FAKESMI_SOURCE /usr/local/lib/joulie/fakesmi The fakesmi binary that every node’s bin/nvidia-smi, bin/rocm-smi and bin/amd-smi link to; the image ships it at the default path. Empty skips the copy, for a run outside the image. KUBECONFIG client-go loading rules The cluster the simulator watches, so it can also run on a workstation; without a kubeconfig it uses the in-cluster configuration. Hardware profiles are the builtin ones in simulator/pkg/hwemu/profiles/, plus local ones from SIM_PROFILES_DIR. The facility values come from the spec’s facility block and fall back to SIM_FACILITY_AMBIENT_TEMP_C, SIM_FACILITY_TEMP_AMPLITUDE_C and SIM_FACILITY_TEMP_PERIOD_H.
A restarted simulator resumes the trees; a tree that no longer matches its spec node stops the start (Restarts and recovery). Details: Configuration notes, Simulator emulate mode.
Helm values of charts/joulie-simulator:
Value Default Effect emulate.enabled false Sets SIM_EMULATE, runs the pod as root with a readiness probe on /readyz, and leaves out SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH: a run starts through the run API, or from a trace set in extraEnv. The chart fails unless replicas is 1. emulate.root /var/lib/joulie-hwemu SIM_HWEMU_ROOT, and a DirectoryOrCreate hostPath mounted at the same path. emulate.tick 1s SIM_EMULATE_TICK. emulate.fuse false Sets SIM_HWEMU_FUSE=true and runs the pod privileged with /dev/fuse and mount propagation Bidirectional on emulate.root, which must be on a shared mount of the host. The emulated agents need agent.emulated.fuse of the Joulie chart. emulate.receiverGate profile SIM_GPU_RECEIVER_GATE. An unquoted on or off, which YAML reads as a boolean, is passed as the word. emulate.clusterSpec "" The spec as text, usually --set-file emulate.clusterSpec=<spec.yaml>, stored in the ConfigMap joulie-simulator-cluster-spec. A changed spec restarts the pod. emulate.clusterSpecConfigMap "" Instead, an existing ConfigMap holding the spec under the key cluster-spec.yaml. Set exactly one of the two. emulate.exporters [] SIM_EXPORTERS, and one ServiceMonitor endpoint per exporter, with honorLabels: false. emulate.nodeSelector joulie.io/hwemu-host: "true" Merged into nodeSelector: the simulator must run on the host whose root the emulated agent pods mount. rbac.workloadRuns auto Whether the ClusterRole carries the rules of a v1 workload run: auto follows emulate.enabled; true and false force them. Any other value fails the render. extraEnv {} Variables merged over env and over the ones the chart sets, so they win. In emulate mode, set SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH here to start an implicit run. The chart always sets POD_NAME from the downward API and mounts its node class, hardware catalog and workload trace ConfigMaps as optional volumes, so a bare install starts without them.
Simulator workloads and scenarios The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) drives a workload trace through the cluster. SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL picks the engine: legacy outside emulate mode, v1 in emulate mode; the two are compared in Workload Simulator. The “Read by” column says which engine reads a variable.
Variable Read by v1 default Legacy default Description SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL both v1 with SIM_EMULATE=true legacy otherwise legacy or v1. v1 without emulate mode and legacy with it stop the start. SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH both (empty) (empty) A trace file, or a directory of them, loaded at startup: legacy replays it, v1 starts it as the implicit run SIM_RUN_ID. The chart sets /etc/joulie-sim-trace/trace.jsonl outside emulate mode; in emulate mode set it in the chart’s extraEnv. SIM_WORKLOAD_TICK legacy 1s Period of the legacy workload loop. An unparsable value, or 0 or less, logs a warning and takes 1s. SIM_WORKLOAD_IMAGE both registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9 the same Container image of every workload pod. SIM_BASE_SPEED_PER_CORE both 1 1 Work units one core, or one GPU, does per second at full speed, so a v3 trace job’s ideal runtime is its durationSec. A run request’s baseSpeedPerCore replaces it. An unparsable value takes 1. SIM_WORKLOAD_OWNER v1 job fixed pod job: one Job object per group; pod: bare pods. SIM_WORKLOAD_INTENT v1 annotation fixed affinity How a pod declares its class: annotation (joulie.io/workload-class), affinity (NotIn [eco] on joulie.io/power-profile for a performance pod), both or none. SIM_WORKLOAD_COMPLETION v1 kwok fixed delete kwok: a finished pod is annotated sim.joulie.io/complete: "true" and the KWOK Stage pod-complete moves it to Succeeded; delete: the pod is deleted. SIM_WORKLOAD_NAMESPACE v1 (empty) Namespace of every pod; empty keeps each trace record’s. SIM_WORKLOAD_NODE_SELECTOR v1 sim.joulie.io/cluster=<spec name> fixed type=kwok key=value pairs, comma separated, added to every pod’s node selector where the trace does not set the key. The default keeps workload pods on the cluster spec’s nodes. SIM_WORKLOAD_TOLERATIONS v1 kwok.x-k8s.io/node=fake:NoSchedule fixed, the same A JSON list of tolerations added to every pod; [] adds none. A GPU vendor’s toleration is added only by the ExtendedResourceToleration admission plugin. SIM_WORKLOAD_JOB_TTL v1 10m ttlSecondsAfterFinished of the Job objects; 0 deletes them as they finish. SIM_WORKLOAD_MAX_CREATES_PER_TICK both -1 (no cap) 20 Pods or Job objects created per tick; a positive count or -1. SIM_WORKLOAD_MAX_DELETES_PER_TICK legacy 10 Finished pods deleted per tick; a positive count or -1. SIM_WORKLOAD_KUBE_QPS, SIM_WORKLOAD_KUBE_BURST both 100, 200 30, 50 Rate limits of the workload’s Kubernetes client. SIM_WORKLOAD_STALL_REPORT v1 5m How long a running job, or the whole run, must make no progress, with every Pending pod Unschedulable, before joulie.sim.job.stalled or joulie.sim.run.stalled. SIM_WORKLOAD_STALL_FORCE_COMPLETE legacy 120s How long a legacy job may make no progress before it is completed by force; -1 disables it. SIM_RUNS_DIR v1 $SIM_HWEMU_ROOT/_runs Directory of the run directories, <SIM_RUNS_DIR>/<run id>/, with the trace and the run’s OTLP files. SIM_RUN_ID v1 run-<UTC yyyymmdd-hhmmss> Id of the implicit run of SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH; no slash, and not . or ... SIM_OTLP_FILE_INTERVAL v1 10s Period of the cumulative metrics snapshot in simulator.metrics.jsonl; one more is written when the run ends. An invalid value stops the start with an error naming the variable, except SIM_WORKLOAD_TICK and SIM_BASE_SPEED_PER_CORE, which fall back to their defaults. A variable only the other engine reads logs a warning naming it.
Run API. In v1 emulate mode the simulator serves one run at a time on its HTTP port; in every other mode these paths answer 412.
Path Method Answer /sim/v1/runs POST Starts a run of runId, from a trace inside SIM_RUNS_DIR, with optional options overriding the settings above. 201 on success; 400 for a bad request or trace; 409 while a run is active or when the run id already has results. /sim/v1/runs/current GET 200 with the active or last run’s status (phase, elapsedSeconds, jobs per state, runStalled); 404 before the first run. /sim/v1/runs/current/finish POST Ends the run; ?cleanup=true also deletes its Job objects or pods. 200 with the final status. Permissions. rbac.workloadRuns adds the permissions a v1 run needs to the joulie-simulator ClusterRole (on pods, batch jobs and joulie.io nodetwins).
KWOK Stage. With SIM_WORKLOAD_COMPLETION=kwok, a pod ends only through the KWOK Stage pod-complete of scripts/simcluster/manifests/stage-pod-complete.yaml, which the simulated cluster applies; on another KWOK cluster apply it too, or set SIM_WORKLOAD_COMPLETION=delete. Details: Configuration notes, Simulator workloads and scenarios.
Scenario runner. scripts/simcluster/scenario.sh (make simcluster-scenario SCENARIO=<file>) has its own settings: Workload Scenarios. So do the other scripts of scripts/simcluster: Simulated Cluster.
Simulator telemetry export In emulate mode the simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) pushes OpenTelemetry metrics of every emulated node and of the facility as OTLP JSON over HTTP, such as to a Prometheus with --web.enable-otlp-receiver. Events are always written to events.jsonl and pushed only with a logs endpoint. Names: Simulator Metrics.
In every mode, GET /otlp/telemetry/{node} and GET /telemetry/{node} serve one node’s OTLP JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest, the format TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT and NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT read. ?format=legacy serves the deprecated packagePowerWatts JSON until v0.4.0; a format other than otlp or legacy answers 400.
Variable Default Description SIM_EXPORTERS (empty) Comma-separated compatibility exporters to serve at /exporters/<name>/metrics: kepler-0.7, kepler-0.12, dcgm-4.8.4, amd-dme-1.5.2 (ROCm device-metrics-exporter v1.5.2). kepler-0.12 serves GPU series only with SIM_KEPLER012_GPU. An unknown name stops the start and lists the valid ones (Compatibility exporters). SIM_KEPLER012_GPU false true makes kepler-0.12 also serve kepler_node_gpu_* for NVIDIA GPUs, as Kepler’s experimental GPU option does. With the chart, set it in extraEnv. SIM_DCGM_HOSTNAME_LABEL hostname Host label of dcgm-4.8.4: hostname, or Hostname as dcgm-exporter releases up to 4.8.2 spell it. SIM_OTEL_FILE_DIR the value of SIM_DEBUG_PERSIST_DIR (default /tmp/joulie-simulator-debug) Directory of events.jsonl, one OTLP JSON LogsData object per line. Empty disables the files. SIM_OTEL_FILE_METRICS false Also append every metrics export to metrics.jsonl in the same directory, one MetricsData object per line. Read with Go’s strconv.ParseBool: 1, t, T, true, TRUE, True, or the same spellings of false; any other value stops the start. POD_NAME the host name Identifies this simulator instance in its own telemetry. The chart sets it from the downward API. OTEL_SDK_DISABLED false true, in any case, turns off both pushes, as the OpenTelemetry specification reads it; any other value leaves them on. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME joulie-simulator service.name of every resource. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (empty) Extra resource attributes, key=value pairs separated by commas. They never override the node and instance attributes. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT (empty) URL of the metrics push, used as is. For Prometheus: http://<prometheus>:9090/api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT (empty) URL of the events push, used as is. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (empty) Base URL for both signals: v1/metrics and v1/logs are appended. A per-signal variable wins. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_COMPRESSION, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL as the specification Headers (key=value,...), timeout in milliseconds, gzip or none, and the protocol, which must be http/json. Each has _METRICS_ and _LOGS_ variants that win for their signal. OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL 60000 Milliseconds between metrics pushes. A rate() window over the pushed counters should cover at least 4 intervals. OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER otlp none turns off that signal’s push. The export follows the OpenTelemetry exporter specification, with http/json only and no default endpoint. A per-signal endpoint is used exactly as given, so it needs the full path. Details: Configuration notes, Simulator telemetry export.
Helm values of charts/joulie-simulator, rendered only when emulate.enabled is true:
Value Default Effect otel.metricsEndpoint "" OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT. otel.logsEndpoint "" OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT. otel.exportIntervalMillis 10000 OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL, in milliseconds since Helm cannot parse durations. otel.resourceAttributes {} OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, joined as key=value pairs. For queries, Prometheus should promote k8s.node.name and host.name onto the data series (otlp.promote_resource_attributes); without that, the node name is joined from target_info. See Prometheus settings.
The simulator chart also ships the Grafana dashboard Joulie - Simulated Cluster (Dashboard), which needs k8s.node.name promoted. These values render whether or not emulate.enabled is true:
Value Default Effect grafanaDashboard.enabled false Renders the ConfigMap joulie-simulator-grafana-dashboard with the dashboard, for a Grafana sidecar that loads dashboards from ConfigMaps. grafanaDashboard.labels grafana_dashboard: "1" Labels of that ConfigMap: the ones the sidecar selects, kube-prometheus-stack’s by default. Simulator hardware profiles The simulator (simulator/cmd/simulator) emulates a node from a hardware profile picked by name: one of the builtin profiles in simulator/pkg/hwemu/profiles/, or a local one.
Variable Default Description SIM_PROFILES_DIR (empty) Directory of local hardware profiles: every *.yaml file directly in it, each with a name equal to its file name without .yaml. Empty, or a directory with no *.yaml, means the builtin profiles only. A missing directory, a *.yml file or a .YAML suffix is an error, never a fallback. A local profile may extend (extends:) a builtin or another local profile, but may not take a builtin’s name. Details: Configuration notes, Simulator hardware profiles.
kubectl plugin The kubectl joulie plugin reads NodeTwin, NodeHardware, Node and Pod objects through your kubeconfig and needs no configuration; without permission to list NodeHardware it shows no hardware. Install: quickstart.
Command Shows kubectl joulie, kubectl joulie status the cluster summary (measured, capped and TDP power, nodes and their power per class, pods per class, average headroom, cooling and PSU stress, PUE) and one row per managed node kubectl joulie top the live dashboard: the status screen refreshed every --interval, with a power sparkline per node; ↑ ↓ select, enter opens the node, p the pods, s sorts, r refreshes, q quits kubectl joulie node <node> one node: hardware, power, twin scores, the caps and governor presets planned and what its agent applied, its pods kubectl joulie pods every pod on a managed node: its class, its node and the node’s class; a performance pod on an eco node is flagged. A pod is performance when it has the joulie.io/workload-class: performance annotation, or a node selector or node affinity on joulie.io/power-profile: performance kubectl joulie version the plugin version Flag Default Meaning -o, --output table json: the same data as one JSON document, for scripts -w, --watch off status and pods: open the live dashboard (-W is an alias) --interval 2s Refresh period of the live dashboard, at least 500ms --no-color off No colors. NO_COLOR=1 does the same, and output that is not a terminal has none -n, --namespace all namespaces pods only: list the pods of this namespace alone, which needs no permission to list pods cluster-wide. The node columns of the live dashboard then count these pods only --kubeconfig, --context, --cluster, --user, --server, --token as kubectl As in kubectl The node table of status and top:
Column Shows NODE The node name HARDWARE The node’s GPUs (count and model) or, on a node without GPUs, its CPUs (sockets and model), from its NodeHardware CLASS The NodeTwin’s schedulable class: performance, eco, draining or unknown POWER The measured node power, and a bar of it against the node’s capped power (its TDP while no cap is known); the power source when nothing measures it TREND The twin’s power trend in W/min; in top, a sparkline of the measured power, each block the share of the capped power it reaches CAP CPU·GPU The effective CPU and GPU caps in percent of the maximum; - for the GPU of a node without GPUs, and for both while the twin has no cap state HEADROOM, COOLING The twin’s predicted power headroom and cooling stress, 0 to 100 CPU, MEM Requested over allocatable, summed over the pods bound to the node that have not finished GPU GPUs requested over allocatable, counting whole GPUs, MIG devices, AMD partitions and shared replicas, each weighted by its share of a GPU; - for a node without GPU resources PODS The pods on the node; ▲n counts its performance pods AGENT The AgentReporting condition: ✓, ✗ with its reason, ? before the controller manager writes it The table drops the columns that do not fit the terminal, in this order: MEM, TREND, HARDWARE, COOLING, HEADROOM.
-o json prints time, summary (nodes per class, pods, performancePods, misplacedPods, podsError, measuredPowerW, cappedPowerW, tdpW, powerTrendWPerMin, avgHeadroomPct, avgCoolingStressPct, avgPsuStressPct, avgPUE, agentsReporting, agentsNotReporting), nodes for status and node (name, class, cpuModel, sockets, gpuModel, gpus, powerSource, measuredPowerW, cappedPowerW, tdpW, powerTrendWPerMin, cpuCapPct, gpuCapPct, headroomPct, coolingStressPct, psuStressPct, cpuRequestedPct, memoryRequestedPct, gpuRequestedPct, pods, performancePods, agentReporting, agentReason) and pods for pods and node (namespace, name, class, node, nodeClass, misplaced, cpu, gpus). cpuCapPct and gpuCapPct are left out while the twin has no cap state yet, and the GPU fields for a node without GPUs. podsError is set when the pods could not be listed; the pod counts are then unknown, not zero. A command’s list is present even when empty ("pods": []).

body:
How Joulie reads power and facility telemetry, and how the agent sends its control intents. Use it to wire Prometheus, an OpenTelemetry producer or the simulator to Joulie. Exported /metrics are on the Metrics Reference; the CRD fields are on CRD and Policy Model.
Backends The same control logic runs on real hardware and on simulator or KWOK clusters; environment variables on the agent choose the wiring, never the hardware identity (that is NodeHardware).
Direction Variable host (default) http none CPU telemetry TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE the node’s RAPL files TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT (HTTP input format) no reading CPU control TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL RAPL and cpufreq files TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL_HTTP_ENDPOINT no writes GPU control TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL nvidia-smi, amdgpu or i915/xe sysfs TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL_HTTP_ENDPOINT no writes Cluster-level inputs come from Prometheus and are read by the controller manager, not the agent: see Input metrics (OpenTelemetry). In host mode the chart mounts the host /sys at /host-sys.
Control intents Action Payload Sent when rapl.set_power_cap_watts capWatts, the node’s CPU total (the simulator splits it over the sockets) a CPU cap in watts, or a percentage the agent can resolve (CPU enforcement algorithm) dvfs.set_throttle_pct throttlePct, 0 to 100 no range to resolve a percentage, TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL_MODE=dvfs, or a refused watt cap; 0 once after an accepted watt cap gpu.set_power_cap_watts capWattsPerGpu, the same for every GPU a GPU cap Each answer and each host write ends as applied, blocked, error or none (no intent) in NodeTwin.status.controlStatus.
Current HTTP contracts Endpoint Serves GET /otlp/telemetry/{node} one OTLP JSON document; point TELEMETRY_CPU_HTTP_ENDPOINT and NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT here GET /telemetry/{node} the same document (?format=legacy: the deprecated JSON, removed in v0.4.0) POST /control/{node} a control intent; answers result, message, state {"node": "worker-01", "action": "dvfs.set_throttle_pct", "throttlePct": 20, "ts": "2026-02-27T00:00:00Z"} HTTP input format The agent (TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE=http) and the controller manager (NODE_POWER_SOURCE=http) read one OTLP JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest per GET, {node} replaced by the node name. Each component’s power is the rate of its hw.energy counter, or its hw.power gauge while the counter warms up; the agent sums the cpu components, the controller manager cpu and gpu (or hw.host.* with NODE_POWER_SCOPE=host). A body without resourceMetrics is read as the legacy JSON, with a warning. The full rules and a minimal document are on the wiki page Telemetry inputs.
Input metrics (OpenTelemetry) The controller manager reads node power (NODE_POWER_SOURCE=prometheus, the chart default) and facility readings (ENABLE_FACILITY_METRICS=true) from Prometheus with PromQL instant queries. Producers push them as OpenTelemetry metrics to Prometheus’ OTLP receiver: the simulator in emulate mode, an OpenTelemetry Collector, or any exporter that follows the table below. Only the controller manager queries Prometheus.
The contract Names come from pkg/otel/semconv; the hw.* names are OpenTelemetry semantic conventions v1.44.0 (Development), the joulie.* names Joulie’s own.
OTel name Unit Instrument Point attributes Prometheus name (default strategy) Read as hw.energy J Counter hw.id, hw.type, hw.name, hw.parent hw_energy_joules_total node power, scope components: rate of the cpu and gpu components hw.power W Gauge the same hw_power_watts node power, scope components: a component without an energy counter hw.host.energy J Counter hw.id=host hw_host_energy_joules_total node power, scope host hw.host.power W Gauge hw.id=host hw_host_power_watts node power, scope host, without an energy counter joulie.facility.ambient_temperature Cel Gauge joulie_facility_ambient_temperature_celsius outdoor ambient temperature (avg) joulie.facility.it.energy J Counter joulie_facility_it_energy_joules_total IT power, as a rate joulie.facility.it.power W Gauge joulie_facility_it_power_watts IT power without an energy counter joulie.facility.cooling.energy J Counter joulie_facility_cooling_energy_joules_total cooling power, as a rate joulie.facility.cooling.power W Gauge joulie_facility_cooling_power_watts cooling power without an energy counter joulie.cooling_zone.ambient_temperature Cel Gauge joulie.cooling_zone.name joulie_cooling_zone_ambient_temperature_celsius ambient temperature of each cooling zone joulie.rack.energy J Counter joulie.rack.name joulie_rack_energy_joules_total power of each rack, as a rate joulie.rack.power W Gauge joulie.rack.name joulie_rack_power_watts power of each rack without an energy counter hw.host.ambient_temperature Cel Gauge hw.id=host hw_host_ambient_temperature_celsius inlet temperature of each node (the hottest sensor) Every producer sets the resource attributes k8s.node.name (the node), service.instance.id (unique per producer and node) and service.name. It reports one cpu component per CPU package and one gpu per GPU, whole-host energy only as hw.host.*, and counters that never decrease. Zone and rack names are the nodes’ joulie.io/cooling-zone and joulie.io/rack labels (Node topology).
The queries Each input is one grouped query per reconcile (node power) or per poll (facility), keyed by node, zone or rack; a node missing from the answer reads source: prometheus-no-data. The otel preset reads the energy rate first and the power gauge only without a counter; kepler and kepler-legacy read Kepler’s node counters. PROMETHEUS_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (auto by default) chooses whether the node label is read from every series or joined from target_info. At start the controller manager logs every query it runs. The full PromQL of each preset, and why it is written that way, is on the wiki page Telemetry inputs.
Name translation strategies Prometheus’ OTLP receiver spells each name under its otlp.translation_strategy, and PROMETHEUS_NAME_TRANSLATION must name the same strategy:
OTel name UnderscoreEscapingWithSuffixes (default) NoUTF8EscapingWithSuffixes UnderscoreEscapingWithoutSuffixes NoTranslation hw.energy hw_energy_joules_total hw.energy_joules_total hw_energy hw.energy hw.power hw_power_watts hw.power_watts hw_power hw.power hw.host.energy hw_host_energy_joules_total hw.host.energy_joules_total hw_host_energy hw.host.energy hw.host.power hw_host_power_watts hw.host.power_watts hw_host_power hw.host.power label k8s.node.name k8s_node_name k8s.node.name k8s_node_name k8s.node.name label hw.type hw_type hw.type hw_type hw.type label hw.id hw_id hw.id hw_id hw.id label joulie.cooling_zone.name joulie_cooling_zone_name joulie.cooling_zone.name joulie_cooling_zone_name joulie.cooling_zone.name label joulie.rack.name joulie_rack_name joulie.rack.name joulie_rack_name joulie.rack.name A producer unit other than J, W, Cel, Hz or 1 changes the suffix and the presets miss the series. The full table is pkg/otel/promname/testdata/prometheus-names.tsv.
Prometheus settings Plain Prometheus, started with --web.enable-otlp-receiver, which serves POST /api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics:
# prometheus.yml storage: tsdb: out_of_order_time_window: 30m # OTLP samples carry the producer's timestamps otlp: promote_resource_attributes: [k8s.node.name, host.name] translation_strategy: UnderscoreEscapingWithSuffixes With the Prometheus Operator, the same through kube-prometheus-stack values (values/prometheus-grafana.yaml sets them; the fields exist in kube-prometheus-stack 91.9.0, prometheus-operator v0.94.1):
prometheus: prometheusSpec: enableOTLPReceiver: true otlp: promoteResourceAttributes: [k8s.node.name, host.name] translationStrategy: UnderscoreEscapingWithSuffixes tsdb: outOfOrderTimeWindow: 30m Install it into the monitoring namespace (helm install telemetry prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack -n monitoring --create-namespace -f values/prometheus-grafana.yaml): the chart’s PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS, http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090, resolves only there.
Prometheus What these inputs need from it 3.0 the --web.enable-otlp-receiver flag, UTF-8 names (NoUTF8EscapingWithSuffixes) 3.4 NoTranslation 3.6 UnderscoreEscapingWithoutSuffixes; target_info over the sample span 3.10 the fix for OTLP sums losing data (prometheus/prometheus#17954): the recommended minimum 3.15 the version tests/promql evaluates the queries in Pitfalls Symptom Cause Fix power reads low just after a producer starts rate() over a series younger than its window wait one PROMETHEUS_RATE_WINDOW pushed counters read a few percent low points arrive late relative to the export interval keep the export interval well above the lag (60 s export, 5m window) PROMETHEUS_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=labels reads no node k8s.node.name not promoted add it to otlp.promote_resource_attributes, or use auto queries fail with HTTP 422 (many-to-many) two producers share a service.instance.id give each producer its own no series at all PROMETHEUS_NAME_TRANSLATION differs from otlp.translation_strategy set them to the same strategy GPU nodes show too much headroom with Kepler Kepler reports GPU energy only from 0.12, behind an experimental flag turn the flag on, or use the otel preset power climbs forever with a custom query a *_joules_total counter read without rate() wrap it in rate() The numbers behind each row are on the wiki page Telemetry inputs.
Grid carbon intensity Joulie ships no carbon intensity provider: point FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_QUERY at one you already export, with FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_UNIT and FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_SIGNAL (marginal or average) (Grid carbon intensity). The reading is converted to gCO2eq/kWh, exported as joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_grams_per_kW_h, and handed to the policy, which does not act on it yet.
Diagnostics The startup log has one input ... line per query. joulie_twin_input_queries_total{input,result} counts each query’s outcome (Twin input metrics), and NodeTwin.status.powerMeasurement.source says whether a node was read.
Next step KWOK and Standalone Modes Workload Simulator Power Simulator The PromQL of every preset, the HTTP format rules, the legacy payload and the producer rules in full: Telemetry inputs on the wiki.
