body:
Every Prometheus metric the agent, the controller manager and the scheduler extender export, for dashboards and alerts. Simulator metrics are on Simulator Metrics; the metrics Joulie reads as input are on Input Telemetry and Actuation Interfaces.
Endpoints by component Component Path Default address Override Agent /metrics :8080 METRICS_ADDR Controller manager /metrics :8081 METRICS_ADDR Scheduler extender /metrics :9877 METRICS_ADDR Agent metrics Backend and selected cap joulie_backend_mode{node,mode} (gauge) mode: none|rapl|dvfs active mode is 1, others 0 joulie_policy_cap_watts{node,policy} (gauge) current selected policy cap in watts RAPL power/energy joulie_rapl_energy_uj{node,zone} (gauge) latest raw RAPL energy counter in microjoules joulie_rapl_estimated_power_watts{node,zone} (gauge) per-zone estimated power from energy deltas joulie_rapl_package_total_power_watts{node} (gauge) sum of package-level estimated power DVFS controller joulie_dvfs_observed_power_watts{node} (gauge) observed package power used by DVFS controller joulie_dvfs_ema_power_watts{node} (gauge) EMA-smoothed power used for decisions joulie_dvfs_throttle_pct{node} (gauge) current throttle percentage joulie_dvfs_above_trip_count{node} (gauge) consecutive above-threshold samples joulie_dvfs_below_trip_count{node} (gauge) consecutive below-threshold samples joulie_dvfs_actions_total{node,action} (counter) action: throttle_up|throttle_down CPU frequency observability joulie_dvfs_cpu_cur_freq_khz{node,cpu} (gauge) current CPU/policy frequency in kHz joulie_dvfs_cpu_max_freq_khz{node,cpu} (gauge) enforced max frequency cap in kHz Governors Written by the agent’s governor control.
joulie_agent_governor_writes_total{node,component,preset,result} (counter) one per governor write: a preset applied, or the baseline restored (preset="baseline") component: cpu|gpu result: applied|applied-unverified|equivalent|unsupported|not-applied|refused|restored|error a reconcile that only checks the setting, and a preset the node cannot express or the agent may not write (disabled), count nothing joulie_agent_governor_state{node,component,preset} (gauge) the preset in effect is 1 (result applied, applied-unverified or equivalent), every other preset of the component 0; all 0 before a write and after a restore Cap results and status writes What the agent reports in the API, for the alerts JoulieCapNotApplied and JoulieAgentWritesBlocked.
joulie_agent_cap_result{node,component,result} (gauge) the result of the last CPU or GPU cap, as the agent writes it to status.controlStatus.<component>.result component: cpu|gpu result: applied|blocked|error|none; the result in effect is 1, the others 0 joulie_agent_status_write_errors_total{node,object} (counter) status writes the API server refused, or that failed to reach it object: NodeTwin (status.controlStatus, caps and governors) or NodeHardware (its status) Reliability joulie_reconcile_errors_total{node} (counter) reconcile-loop errors Policy controller metrics Exported by the controller manager.
FSM state and profile label joulie_policy_node_state{node,state} (gauge) state: ActivePerformance|DrainingPerformance|ActiveEco active state is 1, others 0 joulie_policy_node_profile_label{node,profile} (gauge) controller-manager-applied node label view profile: performance|eco active profile is 1, others 0 Transition accounting joulie_policy_state_transitions_total{node,from_state,to_state,result} (counter) transition events emitted by the controller manager result: applied: transition committed deferred: transition blocked/deferred by safeguards Heterogeneous planning Both are reset every reconcile and computed from the plan after the downgrade guard, so a draining node counts as not performance. family is gpu:<model> when the node has GPUs, otherwise cpu:<model> (see Heterogeneous planning).
joulie_policy_family_nodes{family} (gauge) eligible nodes in each hardware family joulie_policy_family_performance_nodes{family} (gauge) nodes of each hardware family planned in the performance profile Twin input metrics Exported by the controller manager. They show whether the measured inputs (see Input metrics (OpenTelemetry)) are read.
joulie_twin_input_queries_total{input,result} (counter) one increment per Prometheus query of a measured input input: node_power, or the facility input: ambient_temp, it_power, cooling_power, zone_ambient_temp, rack_power, node_inlet_temp, carbon_intensity result: success: every series was read partial: some series were skipped, for a missing key label or a value that is not finite no_data: no usable series error: Prometheus failed the query or could not be reached, or the answer was refused (duplicate keys, several series for a single value) joulie_twin_facility_ambient_temperature_celsius{preset} (gauge) outdoor ambient temperature the facility input last read, in degrees Celsius joulie_twin_facility_it_power_watts{preset} (gauge) IT power the facility input last read, in watts joulie_twin_facility_cooling_power_watts{preset} (gauge) cooling power the facility input last read, in watts joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_grams_per_kW_h{joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_signal} (gauge) grid carbon intensity the facility input last read (FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_QUERY), converted to gCO2eq/kWh joulie_grid_carbon_intensity_signal: marginal or average, from FACILITY_CARBON_INTENSITY_SIGNAL; compare values of one signal only the default Prometheus spelling of the OpenTelemetry metric joulie.grid.carbon_intensity (unit g/(kW.h), grams per kilowatt-hour, attribute joulie.grid.carbon_intensity.signal), a cluster metric with no node label preset is FACILITY_PRESET (otel, legacy or custom). A facility gauge is absent while its input is unknown. PUE is (it_power + cooling_power) / it_power; the overview dashboard’s “Twin inputs” row plots it.
Twin agent coverage Exported by the controller manager, set every reconcile from the AgentReporting condition of each managed node’s NodeTwin (see Managed nodes without an agent).
joulie_twin_nodes_agent_reporting{status,reason} (gauge) managed nodes per condition status and reason status="true", reason="NodeHardwareCurrent": an agent publishes the node’s NodeHardware status="false", reason="NoNodeHardware" or "NodeHardwareStale": no agent has published it, or its last write is more than 15 minutes old; the caps planned there are not enforced all three series are set on every reconcile, so sum(joulie_twin_nodes_agent_reporting{status="false"}) > 0 works as an alert No node label: the nodes are the NodeTwins whose condition is False. The overview dashboard plots the false series in its “Agent: Reliability” row.
Twin health Exported by the controller manager, for the alerts JoulieTwinStale and JoulieNodePowerNoData.
joulie_twin_status_updated_timestamp_seconds{node} (gauge) Unix time of the node’s last NodeTwin status write (status.lastUpdated); time() - joulie_twin_status_updated_timestamp_seconds is the age of the twin joulie_twin_nodes_power_source{source} (gauge) managed nodes per status.powerMeasurement.source of the last reconcile, every source set, 0 included source: prometheus or http with a reading; prometheus-no-data, http-error or http-no-endpoint without one; static when nothing is measured; kepler and utilization are reserved and stay 0 Scheduler extender metrics Request counters joulie_scheduler_filter_requests_total{workload_class} (counter) total filter requests by workload class workload_class: standard|performance joulie_scheduler_prioritize_requests_total{workload_class} (counter) total prioritize (scoring) requests by workload class Request latency joulie_scheduler_filter_duration_seconds{workload_class} (histogram) time to process a filter request joulie_scheduler_prioritize_duration_seconds{workload_class} (histogram) time to process a prioritize request Scoring signals joulie_scheduler_final_node_score{node,workload_class} (gauge) final scheduling score (0-100) for each node and workload class updated on every prioritize call; reflects the combined headroom + cooling + trend + bonus formula joulie_scheduler_node_headroom_score{node} (gauge) power headroom score per node can go negative when projected power (measured + pod marginal) exceeds the capped budget Data freshness joulie_scheduler_stale_twin_data{node} (gauge) 1 if the NodeTwin status is older than the staleness threshold (default 5m), 0 otherwise a node with stale data receives a neutral score (50) instead of its computed value useful for alerting when the controller manager has stopped updating twin status Notes Metrics are scraped, so values move at the scrape interval; the per-CPU frequency series have the highest cardinality.

body:
What to check when you upgrade a Joulie installation from v0.2 to v0.3. Go through the list before running helm upgrade.
Before the upgrade Apply the new CRDs. helm upgrade never updates CRDs, and the API server prunes every field the installed CRD does not know, such as the governor fields. Apply them first:
kubectl apply -f charts/joulie/crds/ Without a checkout, take them from the release chart: helm pull oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie --version <version> --untar --untardir /tmp/joulie-chart, then kubectl apply -f /tmp/joulie-chart/joulie/crds/.
Registry. Point every image.repository under registry.cern.ch/mbunino/joulie at registry.cern.ch/joulie, where charts, images and the plugin are published.
Operator names. The pre-v0.2.0 aliases are gone. Use the image joulie-controller-manager (not joulie-operator), NODE_POWER_* (not OPERATOR_NODE_POWER_*), joulie_policy_* metrics (not joulie_operator_*), and the values key controllerManager: a values file that still sets operator fails the render.
kubectl plugin Scripts. kubectl joulie status prints styled tables and drops columns that do not fit the terminal. A script that parsed its text reads kubectl joulie status -o json instead (fields). Watch. kubectl joulie status -W opens the live dashboard, also kubectl joulie top: q quits it. Install. kubectl krew install joulie. Measured node power Prometheus. The chart sets NODE_POWER_SOURCE=prometheus (preset otel, http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090); without node power data every node reads 0 W with source prometheus-no-data. Set up Prometheus as the quickstart says, or set controllerManager.env.NODE_POWER_SOURCE=static. Kepler. KEPLER_AVAILABLE is gone. Use NODE_POWER_PRESET=kepler (Kepler 0.10 and later) or kepler-legacy (Kepler 0.7 to 0.9). Facility inputs. The default preset is otel; the datacenter_* names need FACILITY_PRESET=legacy (removed in v0.4.0). Replace FACILITY_ZONE_AMBIENT_METRIC_TEMPLATE and FACILITY_RACK_POWER_METRIC_TEMPLATE with FACILITY_ZONE_AMBIENT_TEMP_QUERY and FACILITY_RACK_POWER_QUERY. FACILITY_POLL_INTERVAL of 0 or less stops the controller manager at start. FACILITY_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS defaults to PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS. Deprecated names. Rename the FACILITY_*_METRIC aliases the configuration reference lists; each one read logs a warning. Agents and caps Agents on tainted nodes. The agent tolerates every taint (agent.tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]), so it runs and enforces caps on every node labelled joulie.io/managed=true. To keep it off some, list the taints it may tolerate in agent.tolerations; those nodes then report AgentReporting False. arm64 nodes. Images are published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so arm64 nodes get an agent too; a mirror must copy both platforms. Nodes without an agent. NodeTwin carries the condition AgentReporting (the Agent column of kubectl get nodetwins), False on a managed node no agent publishes NodeHardware for, whose caps are not enforced (Managed nodes without an agent). It needs the new CRDs. CPU of GPU nodes. An eco GPU node gets no CPU cap; only its GPUs take the eco cap. Set CPU_ECO_CAP_ON_UNCAPPABLE_GPU_NODES=true to cap the CPU of a GPU node whose NodeHardware reports no GPU control. Twin GPU budget. A planned GPU cap counts in the twin’s budget only where it applies, so eco nodes whose GPU cap is blocked or error, or that report no GPU control, show less headroom than before (Digital twin). AMD GPU model keys. An AMD node’s model is its product name (amd.com/gpu.product-name, such as AMD_Radeon_PRO_W7900), read before amd.com/gpu.family. Rekey GPU_MODEL_CAPS_JSON and GPU_GOVERNOR_MODEL_PRESETS_JSON entries keyed by a family such as GC_11_0_0. AMD GPU caps. AMD GPUs are now capped through their amdgpu hwmon files under /host-sys, and publish their cap range and gpu.powerDomains in NodeHardware. Keep the chart’s root agent and writable /host-sys, and apply the new CRDs, or a two-die package such as an MI250X keeps a doubled GPU budget. GPU default limit. gpu.capRangePerGpu.defaultWatts is the NVIDIA power.default_limit, which can be below maxWatts: a script or dashboard that took it for the maximum must read maxWatts. A wrapper that answers for nvidia-smi must answer the inventory query, which now ends in power.default_limit. Intel GPU caps. Intel discrete GPUs are now capped through their i915 or xe hwmon files under /host-sys (backend host-intel) and take the eco GPU cap. A values file with its own GPU_PRODUCT_LABEL_KEYS must include gpu.intel.com/product. NVIDIA GPUs without a settable power limit. A GPU whose limits print [N/A] reports blocked instead of error and is named in NodeHardware gpu.warnings; a -pl that prints not supported reports error. Shared, partitioned and DRA GPU nodes. Nodes with MIG devices, time-slicing or MPS replicas, AMD partitions, gpu.intel.com/xe, or a DRA GPU count are GPU nodes: in eco their GPUs take the eco cap and their CPU none. Label a node joulie.io/reserved=true to keep Joulie off it (Shared and partitioned GPUs). GPU product suffixes. Key GPU_MODEL_CAPS_JSON and GPU_GOVERNOR_MODEL_PRESETS_JSON by the GPU product without the -MIG-<profile>, -MIG-INVALID and -SHARED suffixes, such as NVIDIA-H100-NVL. Extender GPU estimate. Pods that request MIG devices, AMD partitions, shared replicas or gpu.intel.com/xe add GPU watts to the extender’s estimate (Scheduler). Governors. Governor control is new and off by default (GOVERNOR_CONTROL, GOVERNOR_WRITES); nothing changes until you turn it on. GPU_GOVERNOR_SUSTAINED_ONLY_MULTI_GPU=true holds sustained only while a pod of 2 or more GPUs runs on the node. See Governor policy. Monitoring and examples Extender metrics. The extender’s Service carries prometheus.io/* annotations (schedulerExtender.service.annotations), so annotation-based discovery starts scraping joulie_scheduler_*. Set the value to {} to keep it unscraped. Example dashboards. The four dashboards under examples/ are gone; the chart’s dashboard (grafanaDashboard.enabled) holds what they showed. Example paths. The examples are six tutorials (examples/01-simulated-cluster to examples/06-cooling-pue). The KWOK cluster of the benchmark experiments moved from examples/07-simulator-gpu-powercaps to experiments/kwok-cluster. Simulator Telemetry format. /telemetry/{node} serves OTLP JSON. Joulie up to v0.2 reading the simulator needs ?format=legacy (removed in v0.4.0), or a v0.3 agent on /otlp/telemetry/{node}. Listen address. Outside a pod the simulator listens on 127.0.0.1:18080. Set SIM_ADDR=:18080 to reach it from other machines; the HTTP API has no authentication. Model values. Nodes the hardware catalogue matches take their peak power and cap ranges from it (an H100 SXM caps between 300 and 700 W instead of 80 and 300 W). Set the variable or the node class key to keep a value. Thermal throttling is off by default; set the SIM_*_THERMAL_THROTTLE_*_C variables to turn it on (Simulator thermal model). Removed knobs. Remove SIM_POD_W, SIM_DVFS_DROP_W_PER_PCT, SIM_GPU_ALPHA_UTIL, SIM_GPU_BETA_CAP and the node class keys podW, dvfsDropWPerPct, noiseStddevW and gpu.powerModel: they are ignored, with one warning each. Results of an older simulator: simulator/CHANGES.md lists every change that moved the numbers, and how far.
Details behind each item: Upgrade notes.

body:
The Joulie chart ships four alerting rules for the failures that leave a cluster looking managed while it is not: a cap that did not apply, an agent that cannot write its status, a stale digital twin, and nodes without measured power. Each has a runbook below that an operator, or an SRE agent, can follow step by step.
Installing the rules The rules live in charts/joulie/alerts/joulie-alerts.yaml, in the Prometheus rule file format. With the Prometheus Operator, turn on the chart’s PrometheusRule:
helm upgrade --install joulie oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie \ --version <version> -n joulie-system \ -f values/joulie.yaml \ --set prometheusRule.enabled=true \ --set prometheusRule.labels.release=kube-prometheus-stack Value Default Effect prometheusRule.enabled false Render the PrometheusRule <release>-joulie-alerts. It needs the PrometheusRule CRD of the Prometheus Operator. prometheusRule.namespace "" (the release namespace) Namespace of the PrometheusRule, one your Prometheus ruleNamespaceSelector selects. prometheusRule.labels {} Labels added to the PrometheusRule, those your Prometheus ruleSelector selects (kube-prometheus-stack selects release: <its release name> by default). Without the operator, load the same file with rule_files. Prometheus must scrape the agent and the controller manager (Metrics); an unscraped component’s alerts cannot fire, so pair these rules with your usual alert on up == 0.
The commands below assume the namespace joulie-system; <node> is the node label of the alert. A node’s NodeTwin and NodeHardware are named after it, lowercased, with every character other than a letter, a digit or a hyphen turned into a hyphen (pkg/api.ObjectNameForNode).
JoulieCapNotApplied Meaning. The CPU or GPU cap planned for a node is not in force: the agent reports result error (the write, or the inventory before it, failed) or blocked (the node offers no way to apply it) in status.controlStatus of the node’s NodeTwin. The node draws more than its profile plans.
Expression. max by (node, component, result) (joulie_agent_cap_result{result=~"error|blocked"}) == 1 for 15 minutes, about 45 agent reconciles, so a transient failure never fires.
Confirm.
kubectl get nodetwin <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.controlStatus}{"\n"}' The cpu or gpu entry names the backend, the result and the reason, for example:
{"cpu":{"backend":"none","message":"RAPL unavailable and DVFS disabled","result":"blocked","updatedAt":"..."}, ...} The agent of the node logs the same reason:
kubectl -n joulie-system logs $(kubectl -n joulie-system get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=joulie-agent \ --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> -o name) | grep -E 'warning|failed' | tail -20 Likely causes.
Result Cause Check blocked, CPU No RAPL power limit files (a VM, no intel-rapl or amd-rapl powercap driver) and no DVFS fallback (no writable cpufreq under /host-sys, no HTTP control backend) kubectl get nodehardware <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.cpu.controlAvailable}' prints false blocked, GPU The GPUs report no settable power limit (NVIDIA boards that print [N/A] for power.limit, Intel GPUs without power1_rated_max) the message names the GPUs; status.gpu.controlAvailable is false error The write failed: a RAPL file refused the value, nvidia-smi -pl refused, an amdgpu or i915 limit did not read back, or an HTTP control backend answered ok: false the message holds the error Fix.
blocked on hardware that cannot be capped: take the node out of NODE_SELECTOR (label joulie.io/managed), or keep it managed and silence the alert for it. On a GPU node whose GPUs cannot be capped, CPU_ECO_CAP_ON_UNCAPPABLE_GPU_NODES=true caps its CPU in eco instead (Power cap configuration). A CPU without RAPL where cpufreq is available: check that the agent mounts the host’s /sys (agent.privileged, the host-sys mount) and that its log has no DVFS controller disabled line, which an invalid DVFS_* setting causes. error: act on the message: a cap outside the hardware’s range (compare capRange and capRangePerGpu in the NodeHardware), a GPU tool missing from the agent image (agent.runtimeClassName, Agent GPU tools), or a driver that refuses limits. The alert clears at the first reconcile that applies the cap.
JoulieAgentWritesBlocked Meaning. The API server refuses the agent’s writes of its own status (the NodeHardware status, or status.controlStatus of the NodeTwin). The caps may still apply, but the twin and kubectl joulie read an old control result, and after 15 minutes without a NodeHardware write the controller manager marks the node AgentReporting=False and treats its caps as not enforced.
Expression. sum by (node, object) (increase(joulie_agent_status_write_errors_total[10m])) > 0 for 20 minutes. A blocked agent fails at least once every 5 minutes, so the alert fires 20 to 25 minutes after the writes start failing, while a single refused write never does.
Confirm.
# when the agent last managed to write kubectl get nodehardware <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.updatedAt}{"\n"}' kubectl get nodetwin <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.controlStatus.cpu.updatedAt}{"\n"}' # whether RBAC lets the agent write kubectl auth can-i patch nodetwins.joulie.io --subresource=status --as=system:serviceaccount:joulie-system:joulie-agent kubectl auth can-i update nodehardwares.joulie.io --subresource=status --as=system:serviceaccount:joulie-system:joulie-agent A timestamp older than 6 minutes while the agent pod runs, or no from kubectl auth can-i, confirms it. A refused NodeHardware write is also in the agent’s log; a refused NodeTwin write is not logged, so the counter and the stale updatedAt are the evidence:
warning: failed to upsert NodeHardware status for node=<node>: nodehardwares.joulie.io "<node>" is forbidden: ... Likely causes.
RBAC: the agent’s ClusterRole lost a verb on nodetwins/status, nodehardwares or nodehardwares/status, or the agent runs under another ServiceAccount than joulie-agent. An admission webhook or policy engine (Kyverno, Gatekeeper) rejects or mutates the write; the error in the log names it. CRDs older than the agent, whose schema rejects a value such as an enum value it does not list. helm upgrade never updates CRDs (Upgrading). The API server throttles or is unreachable from the node (network policy, an overloaded control plane). Fix. Restore the verbs (re-render the chart’s rbac.yaml), exempt the joulie-agent ServiceAccount or the joulie.io resources from the rejecting policy, or apply the running release’s CRDs with kubectl apply -f charts/joulie/crds/. The counter stops growing at the first accepted write; the alert clears 10 minutes later.
JoulieTwinStale Meaning. The controller manager has not written the NodeTwin status of a managed node for more than 10 minutes. The status (schedulableClass, the predicted scores, the measured power, lastUpdated) is frozen: the scheduler extender gives the node a neutral score once lastUpdated is older than TWIN_STALENESS_THRESHOLD (5 minutes), and kubectl joulie shows old numbers.
Expression. time() - max by (node) (joulie_twin_status_updated_timestamp_seconds) > 300 for 5 minutes. A healthy twin is at most a minute or two old; a node planned but never written fires too. If you raise RECONCILE_INTERVAL above 2 minutes, raise the 300 to more than twice the interval.
Confirm.
kubectl get nodetwin <node> -o jsonpath='{.status.lastUpdated}{"\n"}' kubectl -n joulie-system logs deploy/joulie-controller-manager --since=15m | grep -E 'reconcile failed|reconcileNodeTwin|assigned profiles' | tail -20 A healthy controller manager logs assigned profiles policy=... once per reconcile. warning: reconcileNodeTwin <node>: ... names a refused status write of one node; reconcile failed: ... stops every write of that reconcile.
Likely causes.
The status write is refused: RBAC on nodetwins/status for joulie-controller-manager, an admission policy, or CRDs older than the controller manager. The reconcile fails before the twins: a failed list of nodes or of NodeHardware (reconcile failed: list node hardware: ...), or a refused NodeTwin spec write. The loop is stuck or much slower than its interval: API server throttling (KUBE_CLIENT_QPS, KUBE_CLIENT_BURST), or a slow Prometheus. With leader election, the leader lost its Lease and no replica reconciles. When the controller manager is down its series disappear and this alert resolves instead of firing; the alert on its scrape target covers that case.
Fix. Act on the logged error: restore RBAC, exempt the joulie-controller-manager ServiceAccount from the rejecting policy, apply the current CRDs, or raise the client limits. Restart a stuck loop (kubectl -n joulie-system rollout restart deploy/joulie-controller-manager) and keep its log for the bug report. The alert clears at the next written status.
JoulieNodePowerNoData Meaning. For some managed nodes the measured power source returned no reading in the last reconciles: status.powerMeasurement.source of their NodeTwin is prometheus-no-data (no positive reading in the answer to the node power query), http-error (the HTTP endpoint failed) or http-no-endpoint (NODE_POWER_SOURCE=http without NODE_POWER_HTTP_ENDPOINT). Their twins count 0 W, so their headroom and trend are wrong. The alert’s value is the number of nodes.
Expression. max by (source) (joulie_twin_nodes_power_source{source=~"prometheus-no-data|http-error|http-no-endpoint"}) > 0 for 15 minutes, three default rate() windows (PROMETHEUS_RATE_WINDOW), so a new node or a restarted exporter does not fire. static never fires.
Confirm.
kubectl get nodetwins -o custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,SOURCE:.status.powerMeasurement.source kubectl -n joulie-system logs deploy/joulie-controller-manager | grep -E 'node_power|node power' | head -20 Then, in Prometheus, how each node power query ended:
sum by (result) (increase(joulie_twin_input_queries_total{input="node_power"}[15m])) Result Means error Prometheus failed the query or could not be reached no_data the query returned nothing usable success, some nodes at prometheus-no-data those nodes are missing from the answer; run the query from the input node_power: ... startup line to see which nodes it returns Likely causes.
Every node: a wrong PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS, a Prometheus without the OTLP receiver or without k8s.node.name promoted, a translation that does not match PROMETHEUS_NAME_TRANSLATION, or a preset that does not match the exporter (Kepler 0.7 to 0.9 needs NODE_POWER_PRESET=kepler-legacy). The controller manager logs a one-time hint naming which. Some nodes: no power exporter runs there (no RAPL or GPU telemetry, a hypervisor guest), or its series carry another node label than NODE_POWER_NODE_LABEL. http-error: the endpoint is down or answers in another format than OTLP JSON. Fix. Correct the address, the preset or the translation from the hint (Measured node power, Prometheus settings), deploy the exporter on the missing nodes, or silence the alert for nodes that cannot be measured. The alert clears at the first reconcile that reads every node.

What Joulie’s policies do to energy per unit of work on a 40-node CPU cluster (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).
Full report: experiments/01-cpu-only-benchmark/REPORT.md.
Setup Nodes Count CPU Cores Eco cap kwok-cpu-highcore 10 2 x AMD EPYC 9965 384 600 W kwok-cpu-highfreq 10 2 x AMD EPYC 9375F 64 384 W kwok-cpu-intensive 20 2 x AMD EPYC 9655 192 480 W Item Value Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (19 of 40 nodes performance); C: queue-aware Power models SPECpower curves (9655, 9965); analytic model at sockets x TDP (9375F) Eco cap 60 % of sockets x TDP Load CPU utilization 0.55 to 0.58 under A Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime Results Baseline Energy per CPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A CPU work done against A B (static) +2.7 / +1.4 % +2.7 / +1.4 % +0.0 / -0.0 % C (queue-aware) +2.1 / +2.5 % +1.8 / +2.5 % -0.3 / -0.0 % A’s repeat differed by 0.24 % in energy per unit.
Interpretation B and C did the same work as A and used 1.4 to 2.7 % more energy per unit, in all four pairs. Most of the difference is on the EPYC 9375F nodes, which do more of the compute-bound work under B and C. In the simulator every core does the same work, so the 9375F’s higher clock buys nothing (#107), and these results do not show what B and C would do on real hardware.

body:
Joulie is a Kubernetes-native energy management system that uses per-node digital twins to optimize data center power consumption. The twins, fed by real-time telemetry, drive power caps (RAPL, NVML) and scheduling decisions that steer workloads toward the most energy-efficient nodes.
How it works Telemetry feeds the digital twin. The twin drives the controller manager’s decisions: power caps and node profiles. The scheduler extender reads the twin to steer new pods. New placements change the telemetry, closing the loop. What can Joulie do? Trade power for throughput: on 33 simulated H100 NVL nodes, 6 to 9 % less power for 6 to 10 % less GPU work, at about the same energy per unit. Keep performance pods uncapped: a workload-class annotation keeps performance-critical pods on uncapped nodes, where they wait when those nodes are full. Show the energy state: kubectl joulie, a Grafana dashboard and Prometheus metrics. Results so far come from the simulator, whose energy figures do not show what Joulie saves on real hardware: see Experiments and the milestone Evidence-based evaluation.
Where to start Getting Started: concepts, install, configuration Architecture: how the components work Hardware: CPU and GPU support Simulator: a cluster without the hardware Experiments: what the simulator measures

Experiment 05 measures CPU and GPU governor presets as an energy dimension of their own, next to power caps, to choose the defaults Joulie ships. The results come from emulated nodes whose governor and clock physics rest on assumed parameters: they show the shape of each trade-off, not measured savings (#106).
Experiment folder: experiments/05-governor-exploration/. The presets are under Governor presets; governor control is off by default (GOVERNOR_CONTROL, GOVERNOR_WRITES, Configuration reference).
Questions Q1: per CPU driver, which preset minimises energy to solution at each load, and at what cost in time? Q2: per GPU family and workload kind, energy and time of each GPU preset, alone and with a 60 % cap? Q3: with a receiver gate, how much do multi-GPU jobs gain from sustained? Q4: at cluster level, do governors beat caps alone on energy without breaking the performance class? Q5: which conclusions survive the assumed parameters? A default passes on a profile when it lowers energy with a p95 slowdown of at most 5 % (performance class) and 20 % (eco class), in Tier A, in Tier B and at every value Q5 sweeps.
Method Tier A: simulator/cmd/govsweep, an offline sweep in virtual time, one fresh emulated node per cell, presets planned by pkg/governor as the agent plans them. Grid: five CPU profiles (one per frequency driver) and five GPU profiles, every preset, idle, steady and bursty loads, jobs on 1 to 4 GPUs, two seeds. Measure: the node’s energy to solution and the job’s time, as medians against the baseline arm (performance with boost on; auto with no cap). Tier B: one arm on a simulated cluster with Joulie in the loop, checking presets, results and restore. Run: 2026-10-28, 11,410 Tier A cells. Tier B Arm all on a 16-Node simulated cluster passed every check (TestSimclusterE2E, GS01 to GS04): each result matched the mapping, and every file was restored after GOVERNOR_CONTROL=off. Workload runs per arm (Q4) are not part of this experiment.
Reproduce Tier A runs on one machine, with no Kubernetes:
experiments/05-governor-exploration/scripts/run_tier_a.sh [config] [out] config defaults to configs/tier-a.yaml (configs/tier-a-sensitivity.yaml is the Q5 grid, configs/tier-a-gate.yaml the Q3 one) and out to a new directory under ~/.cache/joulie/experiments/05/; the script writes summary.md there. Tier B needs Docker, as the simulated cluster does:
SIMCLUSTER_NAME=joulie-sim-gov experiments/05-governor-exploration/scripts/run_tier_b.sh all The other arms, the settings and the result files are in the experiment README.
Assumptions GPU idle costs: dataPathHoldW (10 W per GPU) and gatingOffIdleW (20 W) set what sustained and peak cost. GPU clock response: clockBeta and memoryKneeFrac set what efficient saves and costs. The receiver gate is off, with neutral fractions. CPU: idleGovernorDeltaW, eppGain, eppCeilingDrop and the 500 ms freqRampMS. The MI300X’s lowest cap (minW 0 W) and the class intensities of the job model. The measurements that would settle each, the per-profile tables and the full discussion: Governor exploration.

What Joulie’s policies do to energy per unit of GPU work on a 41-node cluster of five GPU families (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).
Full report: experiments/02-heterogeneous-benchmark/REPORT.md.
Setup Nodes Count GPUs per node kwok-h100-nvl 12 8 x NVIDIA H100 NVL kwok-h100-sxm 6 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 kwok-l40s 7 4 x NVIDIA L40S kwok-mi300x 2 8 x AMD Instinct MI300X kwok-w7900 6 4 x AMD Radeon PRO W7900 CPU-only (EPYC 9965, 9375F, 9655) 8 none Item Value Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (31 of 41 nodes performance); C: queue-aware Eco cap 70 % of each GPU’s maximum Cap response exponent fitted per family to published data: H100 SXM 0.43, H100 NVL 0.50, MI300X 0.62, L40S 1.20, W7900 1.0 (no data) Load GPU utilization 0.46 to 0.49 under A Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime Results Baseline GPU-node energy per GPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A GPU work done against A Pending performance jobs (A: 0.7) B (static) +0.1 / +4.6 % +3.6 / +3.0 % +3.6 / -1.4 % 3.5 C (queue-aware) +1.2 / +2.9 % -1.0 / +0.8 % -2.3 / -2.1 % 5.8 A’s repeat differed by 0.56 % in energy per unit.
Interpretation B and C did not lower GPU-node energy per unit of work at this load, in all four pairs, and kept more performance jobs waiting. The difference comes from placement: more of the GPU work runs on the MI300X and the H100 NVL, which cost more per unit in the simulator. The simulator gives every GPU the same speed whatever its power (#107), so these per-family costs are not those of real hardware.

body:
What Joulie’s policies do to power and energy per unit of GPU work on a 41-node cluster of H100 NVL nodes (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).
Full report: experiments/03-homogeneous-h100-benchmark/REPORT.md.
Setup Item Value Nodes 33 H100 NVL nodes (8 GPUs each) and 8 CPU-only nodes Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (27 of 41 nodes performance); C: queue-aware Eco cap 280 W, 70 % of 400 W Cap response computeGamma 0.50, the H100 PCIe’s published response, since the NVL has no published data (#106) Load GPU utilization 0.55 to 0.58 under A Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime Results Baseline GPU-node energy per GPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A GPU work done against A Pending performance jobs (A: 0.7) B (static) +0.5 / -0.2 % -5.7 / -7.1 % -6.5 / -7.5 % 9.2 C (queue-aware) +0.3 / +0.7 % -5.8 / -8.8 % -6.4 / -10.0 % 9.8 A’s repeat differed by 0.01 % in energy per unit. B and C were not repeated, so their own noise is unknown (#113).
Interpretation B and C traded power for throughput: 6 to 9 % less power and 6 to 10 % less GPU work, with more performance jobs waiting, at about the same energy per unit of work. The capped GPUs’ lower dynamic energy per unit is cancelled by the GPU nodes’ idle power spread over less work. On the 8 CPU-only nodes energy per unit rose by 3 to 7 %, as in the CPU-only benchmark.

Not a valid result. Its results do not stand and are not published. The experiment is to be redone on the scheduling logic extracted into an importable library (#122), as a behaviour scenario (#115).
An audit found that jobs that do not fit are dropped instead of queued, energy is divided by the placed jobs only, the arms are mislabelled, the selected formula never ran through the cooling model, and the formula was chosen and reported on the same 8 seeds. The scripts are Python models of the cluster, the cooling and the formula; they import no Joulie code and do not follow changes to the extender.
Objective Test whether Joulie’s energy-aware scheduling formula beats Kubernetes bin packing (MostAllocated) on energy, with a Modelica FMU (DXCooled Airside Economizer) for the cooling and PUE, on a 28-node cluster (formula tuning) and a 2,500-node one (main runs).
Scheduler Description BASELINE Kubernetes MostAllocated (bin packing by allocation ratios) JOULIE projected headroom (marginal power baked in) + cooling stress + adaptive trend (+/-25) JOULIE-legacy power headroom + estimated pod power + idle GPU penalty + adaptive trend Folder: experiments/04-scoring-formula-validation/. The method, both formulas and the scripts: Benchmark experiments.
